Sitting superintendents will withdraw if unsuccessful finalist applications jeopardize their current jobs.
A 10-to-12-person representative community panel under NDAs still incorporates student, parent, and educator perspectives.
disagreements.resolution: Millicent Rogers amended her original motion (accepted by seconder Emily Chávez) to adopt Option B—confidential finalist panels with signed confidentiality agreements and no public release of finalist names—passing 7-0.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 5/9/24
meetings.executive_summary: During its May 9, 2024 work session (moderated by Millicent Rogers with Chair Bettina Umstead present and Natalie Beyer participating virtually), the Board of Education unanimously approved consent items, the 2024 Legislative Agenda, and a June 2024 LGBTQIA+ Pride Month Proclamation, and voted 7-0 to modify its FY 2024-25 county budget request to $27.4 million to raise EC self-contained supplements to $350/month and cover 44 DHH/language facilitator positions and the $7,000 EC facilitator bonus. The board also reviewed major informational reports on ARP/ESSER III closeout (~$7M projected carryover amid urgent HVAC/maintenance needs), a 10-year student enrollment forecast (+4,800 students requiring ~$500M in new seats), and 2022-23 student discipline data (7.9% short-term suspension rate and 15% suspension rate for students with disabilities). Members debated whether to move directly to a Pre-K–3 short-term suspension ban before the new school year—as urged by Jovonia Lewis—or build supportive alternatives first alongside a Code of Conduct Task Force, and approved the May 9 personnel report 6-0 after closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Approval, and April 11, 2024 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a moment of silence and Teacher Appreciation Week recognition, the board approved the May 9 work session agenda (7-0 on roll call, moved by Alexandra Valladares and seconded by Emily Chávez) and the April 11, 2024 minutes (7-0 on roll call, moved by Alexandra Valladares and seconded by Jessica Carda-Auten), with Natalie Beyer participating virtually.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Ten speakers addressed Growing Together hardship transfer denials/appeals for Birch Avenue/E.K. Powe families and Lakewood over-enrollment (Caroline Asher, Jenna Crowther); demands to release superintendent finalist bios and hold public community finalist interviews (Lauren Sartain, Girdre Mahajan, Brian Calloway); tiny-home workforce housing on Northern High School land (Frederick Raven); disproportionate suspensions of students with disabilities at 15% (Eliza Strickland, Dr. Jennifer Gierisch, Kristen Southworth); and calls to renovate downtown DSA instead of relocating (Matt Kopac).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda and 2024 Legislative Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved consent items 7-0 (moved by Alexandra Valladares, seconded by Emily Chávez) and then unanimously adopted the 2024 Legislative Agenda 7-0 (moved by Jovonia Lewis, seconded by Jessica Carda-Auten), with Valladares urging community engagement to support Durham's legislative delegation.

agenda_items.title: LGBTQIA+ Pride Month Proclamation (June 2024)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members read aloud the June 2024 LGBTQIA+ Pride Month Proclamation citing DPS's Gender Support Policy, Stonewall history, and North Carolina's SB 49 and HB 574. Jovonia Lewis asked legal counsel whether the proclamation complied with state statutes (Parents' Bill of Rights); counsel confirmed a resolution creates no statutory violation, and the board adopted the proclamation 7-0 on roll call.

agenda_items.title: Operations Services: ARP / ESSER III Closeout Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reported that of $109.7M in ESSER III funds expiring September 30, 2024 (liquidated December 31), ~12–13% ($14M) remained unspent as of April 30 with ~$7M projected carryover prioritized for curriculum resources, Panorama software, and ~$6–7M in facilities/HVAC repairs, while gaggle software funds reverted to the state and six summer programs rely on ESSER. Board members stressed urgent HVAC repairs (~$10M immediate need, ~$900M long-term capital need) ahead of July year-round school openings.

agenda_items.title: Operations Services: DPS Student Enrollment 10-Year Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Matthew Palmer, Kristen Brookshire, and Durham City-County Planning staff presented a 10-year enrollment forecast projecting +4,800 students—concentrated in eastern/southeastern Durham—that would push DPS past its 35,000-seat capacity and require nearly $500M in new seats (~$100K per seat) under HB 90 K–3 class-size caps. Staff noted North Carolina prohibits developer impact fees and restricts SAPFOs, prompting board members to urge interlocal agreements, a joint City-County-DPS task force, East Durham land banking, and regular four-year bonds.

agenda_items.title: Student Support Services: Discipline Data & Restorative Practices Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Maddox-Perry presented 2022-23 DPI discipline data showing a peak 7.9% short-term suspension rate, 7.5% Restorative Practice Center (RPC) assignments, 93 long-term suspended students not enrolling in alternative options, and high suspension rates for students with disabilities, alongside a three-pronged MTSS/RPC/SEL/mental-health plan and a recommendation to overhaul Policy 4301 (Character, Conduct & Support). Board members demanded granular intersectional data and Lakeview metrics, supported forming a Code of Conduct Task Force including practitioners and neurodivergent advocates by June/August, and split over whether to pursue an immediate Pre-K–3 suspension ban before the task force.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Amendment and Modified FY 2024-25 Budget Request (EC/ESL Supplements)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead moved and Emily Chávez seconded amending the agenda (passed 7-0) to hear Interim Superintendent Moore's budget update ahead of county submission. Moore reported that accounting for vacancies raised the $200/month EC/ESL teacher supplement from $950K to $1.1M, leaving $400K of the board's $1.5M addition; staff proposed raising EC self-contained teachers to $350/month (~127 teachers, ~$200K), adding $200/month for ~44 sign language/DHH/visually impaired/spoken language positions, and continuing the $7,000 EC facilitator bonus under a modified $27.4M request, which passed 7-0 on roll call.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and May 9, 2024 Personnel Action Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At 03:42:16, the board voted 7-0 by roll call to enter closed session for approximately two hours and 21 minutes. Returning to open session at 06:04:12, the board approved the May 9, 2024 personnel action report by a 6-0 voice vote before adjourning at 06:04:58.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 5/9/24
disagreements.issue: Immediate Pre-K–3 Short-Term Suspension Ban vs. Phased On-Ramp and Task Force Review
disagreements.summary: Following sobering 2022-23 discipline data showing a 7.9% overall short-term suspension rate and 15% rate for students with disabilities, Jovonia Lewis urged drafting a policy ban on Pre-K–3 short-term suspensions before the new school year, while Deputy Superintendent Dr. Nicholas King and other board members favored building supportive alternatives and convening a Code of Conduct Task Force first.
disagreements.side_a_position: Direct staff immediately to draft a policy eliminating short-term out-of-school suspensions for Pre-K through third grade before the 2024-25 school year starts.
side_a_arguments: Some elementary principals already refrain from suspending young children while others continue doing so, creating inequitable outcomes across schools.
Waiting for a full task force risks starting another school year under inconsistent practices.
disagreements.side_b_position: Avoid an immediate outright ban without first equipping school staff with training, structures, and a multi-stakeholder Policy 4301 task force.
side_b_arguments: Deputy Superintendent Dr. Nicholas King cited research indicating districts that imposed immediate bans without trained alternatives experienced worse outcomes.
Bettina Umstead and Emily Chávez favored an 'additive and subtractive' on-ramp that installs restorative supports alongside forming a Code of Conduct Task Force by June to convene in August.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote; Chair Bettina Umstead agreed to work with staff to return with a proposed timeline and framework for the Policy 4301 task force and supportive practices.

meetings.executive_summary: At its April 25 monthly meeting chaired by Bettina Umstead, the Board of Education approved the $325,810 demolition and abatement Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) for the new Durham School of the Arts site despite extensive public comment from Durham for DSA advocates urging a pause to renovate downtown instead. After Comptroller Carrie Crutchfield presented updated classified salary range recommendations, the Board declined a formal vote in favor of informal modeling consensus using 45% to 55% pay ranges. The Board then unanimously added a $200/month supplement for EC and ESL teachers (7-0), directed staff to return a $1.5 million hard-to-staff equity plan inclusive of those supplements (6-0), and adopted the FY 2024-25 proposed local budget request (6-0).

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead called the meeting to order and led student recognitions and district celebrations prior to formal business.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review, Minutes Tabling, Consent Agenda, and Legislative Agenda Deferral
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board approved the meeting agenda, tabled the March 21, 2024 monthly meeting minutes for typographical and vote-tally corrections, approved Consent Agenda Items A-H, and deferred the Board Legislative Agenda to the May 9 work session.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Agenda Approved 7-0; Minutes Tabled 7-0; Consent Approved 7-0; Legislative Deferral Approved 7-0

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment (Durham for DSA and Community Speakers)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Multiple Durham for DSA speakers urged the Board to pause spending on the Duke Homestead Road site and renovate downtown DSA to save tens of millions of dollars for deferred 2022 bond elementary schools including Club Boulevard, Morehead, Mangum, and Bethesda.

agenda_items.title: New Durham School of the Arts Demolition and Abatement GMP Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Operational Services staff presented the $325,810 Guaranteed Maximum Price contract with Monteith Construction / Balfour Beatty Joint Venture in association with Right Build International for demolition and abatement on the Duke Homestead Road property. Board members acknowledged public concerns over rising construction costs while approving the site preparation contract.

agenda_items.title: Classified Salary Study and Pay Range Modeling (Carrie Crutchfield)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Comptroller Carrie Crutchfield presented revised classified compensation ranges comparing surrounding districts, hold-harmless protections at 2022-23 plus 11%, and individualized pay notice concepts. Board members objected to taking a formal vote on preliminary figures and instead gave informal thumbs-up consensus to model 45% to 55% pay ranges.

agenda_items.title: FY 2024-25 Budget Adoption, EC/ESL Supplements, and $1.5M Hard-to-Staff Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board reviewed budget Q&A responses and debated whether to earmark a flat $200/month supplement specifically for EC and ESL teachers or adopt a flexible $1.5 million hard-to-staff allocation. The Board passed the $200/month EC/ESL supplement 7-0, added an inclusive $1.5 million hard-to-staff equity plan 6-0, and adopted the FY 2024-25 local budget ask 6-0.

Emily Chávez seconded the deferral motion. The Board approved the deferral 7-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approve New Durham School of the Arts Demolition and Abatement GMP ($325,810) with Monteith Construction / Balfour Beatty Joint Venture
votes.notes: Joint venture in association with Right Build International for the Duke Homestead Road site; transcript ASR also cites ~$325,800.
votes.discussion_detail: Following passionate public comment from Durham for DSA advocates arguing that renovating downtown DSA (~$183M estimate) would cost far less than building at Duke Homestead Road (~$241M-$256M) and preserve funds for 2022 bond elementary schools, staff presented the $325,810 demolition and abatement GMP with Monteith Construction / Balfour Beatty Joint Venture and Right Build International. votes.item_title: Add $200/Month Supplement for EC Teachers and ESL Teachers to FY 2024-25 Proposed Budget
votes.notes: Estimated cost ~$762,000 for 287 EC teachers and ~$192,000 for 96 ESL teachers prior to filling vacancies.
votes.discussion_detail: Responding to extensive advocacy from Durham Association of Educators members, parents, and EC/ESL educators over high vacancy rates, Jessica Carda-Auten moved to add a $200/month supplement for EC and ESL teachers into the FY 2024-25 budget request, seconded by Millicent Rogers. Emily Chávez and Jovonia Lewis strongly backed establishing a guaranteed floor for these hard-to-fill roles, while Natalie Beyer, Bettina Umstead, and Alexandra Valladares raised concerns about leaving out EC/ESL instructional assistants, related service providers, and other critical positions without broader equity data. Millicent Rogers also cautioned against last-minute non-reimbursable local salary commitments before calling the question. Despite differing views on scope, the Board voted 7-0 to pass the targeted EC and ESL teacher supplement.

votes.item_title: Direct Administration to Develop Equity-Focused $1.5 Million Plan for Hard-to-Staff Positions (Inclusive of EC/ESL $200/Month Supplement)
ayes: All present members (6 present; one member absent at time of vote)
votes.notes: Tally shifted from 7-0 at 04:09:48 to 6-0 at 04:18:06 indicating one board member stepped out or departed prior to this vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately after adopting the $200/month EC and ESL teacher supplement, Natalie Beyer moved to direct administration to return a comprehensive $1.5 million plan—inclusive of the EC/ESL teacher supplement—to support hard-to-staff positions through an equity lens. Millicent Rogers seconded the motion, noting that expanding the allocation to $1.5 million would give staff flexibility to address related service providers, instructional assistants, or other acute shortage categories identified through district data. Board members agreed that pairing the $200/month teacher floor with an additional ~$500,000+ equity pool bridged the divide between targeted and holistic compensation strategies. With six members present, the motion carried 6-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Superintendent's Proposed FY 2024-25 Local Budget Request Plus $1.5 Million Hard-to-Staff Addition
ayes: All present members (6 present; one member absent at time of vote)
votes.notes: Adds $1.5M hard-to-staff supplement pool onto Superintendent Catty Moore's ~$26M proposed local budget request.
votes.discussion_detail: Following the addition of the $1.5 million hard-to-staff equity allocation, Natalie Beyer moved to adopt Superintendent Catty Moore's proposed FY 2024-25 local budget request as amended with the additional $1.5 million. Jessica Carda-Auten seconded the motion so the Board's formal funding request could be transmitted to the Durham County Manager and Board of County Commissioners on schedule. No further debate occurred on the final budget package. The Board passed the proposed budget 6-0 by voice vote.

ayes: All present members (6 present; one member absent at time of vote)
votes.discussion_detail: After concluding budget action, Chair Bettina Umstead called for a motion to enter closed session pursuant to the statutory exemptions stated on the agenda. ayes: All present members (6 present; one member absent at time of vote)

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 4/25/24
disagreements.issue: Targeted $200/Month EC & ESL Teacher Supplement vs. Broader $1.5M Flexible Hard-to-Staff Equity Pool
disagreements.summary: Board members debated whether to mandate an immediate $200/month flat supplement restricted to certified EC and ESL teachers or allocate a larger, flexible $1.5 million hard-to-staff pot informed by staffing equity data.
disagreements.side_a_position: Guarantee an explicit $200/month supplement for EC and ESL teachers immediately in the proposed budget.
side_a_arguments: Honors sustained public advocacy from DAE, EC parents, and ESL educators facing severe vacancy crises.
Establishes a concrete floor for two highest-need classroom teacher groups without further delay.
disagreements.side_b_position: Prioritize a flexible $1.5 million hard-to-staff equity plan guided by administration data rather than locking in an ad hoc single-role supplement.
side_b_arguments: Excludes EC instructional assistants, therapists, nurses, and other hard-to-fill staff if restricted solely to certified EC/ESL teachers.
Adding non-reimbursable local supplements late in the budget process risks unintended inequities across employee groups.
disagreements.resolution: The Board passed both measures in sequence: first approving the $200/month EC/ESL teacher supplement (7-0) and then approving a $1.5 million hard-to-staff equity plan inclusive of the EC/ESL supplement (6-0).

disagreements.issue: Formal Board Approval vs. Informal Modeling Direction for Classified Salary Min/Max Ranges

disagreements.side_a_position: Do not take a formal vote on preliminary salary ranges that could create false expectations or confusion before county funding is known.
side_a_arguments: Public and staff still have unresolved questions about individual placement and neighboring district comparisons.
Formal votes on preliminary concepts risk repeating the October salary rollout miscommunication.
disagreements.side_b_position: Give staff clear board direction on pay-range width so modeling and individualized pay notices can proceed.
side_b_arguments: Staff need guidance on 45% to 55% range assumptions to prepare modeling for employees ahead of county budget negotiations.
disagreements.resolution: Resolved at 02:56:03 through informal thumbs-up consensus directing staff to model 45% to 55% ranges without taking a formal vote.

disagreements.resolution: Resolved through consensus edits revising 'Minimum' to 'Desired Qualifications' while retaining rigorous competency expectations for finance, equity, and district leadership; approved 6-0.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Special Meeting | 4/10/24
disagreements.issue: Board Liaison Structure and North Carolina Open Meetings Law Compliance
disagreements.summary: Board members and counsel debated whether designating two board members as interim liaisons to Alma Advisory Group posed legal risks under Open Meetings Law or concentrated influence compared to routing communications solely through the Chair.
disagreements.side_a_position: Allow two board liaisons (or open interest across members) with clear guardrails to ensure broader representation and backup capacity.
side_a_arguments: Two liaisons provide continuity if one member has scheduling conflicts.
Allowing other interested members—including outgoing members like Alexandra Valladares—prevents concentrating search communication solely in the Chair and Vice Chair.
disagreements.side_b_position: Limit interim point-of-contact duties to the Chair (or Chair/Vice Chair) or defer liaison selection to avoid Open Meetings Law complications and premature decisions.
side_b_arguments: Chair typically handles routine vendor logistics and polling under board practice without needing a separate subcommittee.
Attorney Bloomberg noted legal review is prudent if multiple members act on behalf of the Board between noticed meetings.
disagreements.resolution: Per Millicent Rogers's and Alexandra Valladares's suggestion, the Board held off naming formal liaisons that evening and asked Chair Bettina Umstead and Vice Chair Emily Chávez to check individually with board members ahead of the next meeting (resolved April 11 with Chair and Vice Chair serving as points of contact).

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 3/21/24
disagreements.issue: Impacts of Districtwide Community Eligibility Provision (CEP) Rollout on Title I School Allocations
disagreements.summary: Following staff's recommendation to apply for districtwide free breakfast and lunch under CEP, Alexandra Valladares and administration exchanged contrasting perspectives on five schools losing Title I status.
disagreements.side_a_position: Highlight the 'Tale of Two Cities' nuance that shifting Title I identification strips flexible Title I staffing/Pre-K dollars from five schools (Creekside, Mangum, Club Boulevard, Morehead, George Watts).
side_a_arguments: Removing Title I status eliminates funds principals used to supplement positions like community schools coordinators and Pre-K IAs.
Acknowledged federal lowering of the CEP threshold from 40% to 25% made districtwide CEP newly feasible this year rather than blaming staff for past inaction.
disagreements.side_b_position: Clarify that the five schools' Title I exit is driven independently by declining ISP poverty percentages below 35%, not by adopting districtwide CEP.
side_b_arguments: Those five schools were exiting grandfathering regardless of CEP because their direct-certification ISP dropped below federal Title I thresholds.
Districtwide CEP saves ~$1.5M in nutrition operations, eliminates meal debt, and brings in federal reimbursements while preserving rank-ordered Title I equity.
disagreements.resolution: Administration clarified the Title I grandfathering mechanics and received Board consensus support to proceed with the districtwide CEP application (no formal vote required).

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Meeting | 3/13/24
disagreements.issue: Conflict-of-Interest Scrutiny, Political Ties, and Microaggression Dispute During Search Firm Screening
disagreements.summary: A sharp disagreement arose when Alexandra Valladares questioned perceived political and local connections among search firm bidders—specifically referencing Durham City Council Member Javiera Caballero's former work at Alma Advisory Group—prompting pushback from Natalie Beyer over singling out firms and culminating in a point of personal privilege.
disagreements.side_a_position: Examine political, elected-official, and local connections across search firms transparently to avoid conflicts of interest or public mistrust.
side_a_arguments: Community trust requires scrutinizing whether elected officials or former Durham consultants have ties to bidding firms such as Alma, alongside noting staff ties to NCSBA.
Dismissing these transparency concerns as a 'conspiracy theory' constitutes a microaggression rather than addressing legitimate governance questions.
disagreements.side_b_position: Apply neutral conflict-of-interest standards evenly across all bidders without singling out one firm or relying on speculation.
side_b_arguments: Legal conflict thresholds (such as statutory 10% ownership/family rules cited by Attorney Rod Malone) govern disqualifications, and multiple firms have former public education connections.
Speculative claims about one firm risk tainting the RFP review unfairly.
disagreements.resolution: Following Valladares's point of personal privilege, Natalie Beyer apologized at 00:40:49 for the phrase used, Attorney Rod Malone clarified statutory conflict thresholds, and the Board agreed by consensus at 00:44:37 to bar any vendor communications outside designated contact Dr. Tanya Giovanni before shortlisting NCSBA, Alma, BWP, and Summit.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Work Session | 3/7/24
meetings.executive_summary: Presiding as Work Session Chair, Jovonia Lewis led the March 7 work session in which the Board amended its agenda to add a Personnel Report (7-0), approved prior minutes and the Consent Agenda (7-0), unanimously voted to join multi-district federal social media litigation against Meta, ByteDance, Snap, and Google (7-0), approved transferring $12,421,277 in 2022 General Obligation Bond funds (7-0), and authorized finalization of the Turner & Townsend Heery facility conditions assessment contract (7-0). The Board also held an extensive FY 2024-25 budget priorities discussion—featuring a policy debate over Vice Chair Emily Chávez's proposal to shift once-a-week elementary World Language spending toward Dual Language Immersion, EC/ESL/bilingual stipends, and districtwide CEP—before receiving a Growing Together implementation update and adopting the Arts in Our Schools Month Proclamation (6-0).

agenda_items.title: Agenda Amendments, Minutes Approval, Public Comment, and Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board amended the agenda to add the March 7 Personnel Report to Consent (7-0), approved February 7-8 and revised January 25 minutes (7-0), heard public comments on Growing Together hardships and classified salaries, and adopted the Consent Agenda (7-0).

agenda_items.title: FY 2024-25 Budget Priorities, Program Evaluation, and Staff Supplements Debate
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Administration and Board members reviewed budget priorities, ESSER cliff risks, and program evaluations. Emily Chávez sparked debate by questioning once-a-week World Language expansion in favor of Dual Language Immersion and equity investments for Black, Latinx, EC, and ESL students, while members requested cost data on EC/ESL/bilingual stipends and districtwide CEP.

agenda_items.title: Multi-District Social Media Litigation Presentation and Contingency Retainer Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Attorney Janet Ward Black (representing Ward Black Law, Baird Mandalas, and Lieff Cabraser) outlined federal multi-district litigation against Meta, ByteDance, Snap, and Google over youth mental health harms modeled on Juul settlements. The Board voted 7-0 to join the litigation and approve the contingency fee retainer.

agenda_items.title: 2022 General Obligation Bond Fund Transfer ($12,421,277) and DSA Transit Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Frederick Davis updated the Board on Murray-Massenburg, Glenn, DSA, Holt, and Morehead bond projects and construction inflation. After questioning GoDurham bus access for DSA and confirming deferred elementary schools remain safe, the Board approved the $12,421,277 capital project ordinance transfer 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Turner & Townsend Heery Long-Range Facility Conditions Assessment Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and consultants from Turner & Townsend Heery and DLR Group presented their comprehensive 6-to-8-month assessment covering all six million square feet of DPS schools and administrative facilities with racial equity, HVAC/MERV-13, and sustainability metrics. The Board voted 7-0 to finalize contract edits for the March 21 consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: Growing Together Implementation, Lottery, and Student Assignment Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff detailed pre-K/EC classroom continuum alignments, lottery placements, legacy sibling transfers, year-round intersession camps, and after-school care coordination across 56 schools while addressing parent portal confusion.

agenda_items.title: Arts in Our Schools Month Proclamation (March 2024), Follow-Up Summary, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Arts supervisor Lester Turner introduced and Board members read the Arts in Our Schools Month Proclamation, passing 6-0. After reviewing follow-up items with Dr. Nicholas King, the Board entered closed session (6-0) and adjourned at 06:16:03.

votes.item_title: Approve Work Session Agenda as Amended
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately after amending the agenda to include the March 7 Personnel Report, Presiding Chair Jovonia Lewis requested approval of the full agenda as amended. Millicent Rogers moved approval, and Natalie Beyer seconded. No further modifications were raised. All seven members approved the amended agenda 7-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approve Meeting Minutes from February 7 and February 8, 2024
votes.discussion_detail: The Board reviewed the draft minutes from its February 7 and February 8, 2024 meetings. Millicent Rogers moved approval of both sets of minutes, and Natalie Beyer seconded the motion. No revisions or objections were noted by members. The voice vote passed unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Approve Revised Meeting Minutes from January 25, 2024
votes.discussion_detail: Presiding Chair Jovonia Lewis presented the revised minutes from the January 25, 2024 meeting for Board action. Natalie Beyer moved approval of the revised January 25 minutes, and Millicent Rogers seconded the motion. No further changes were requested. The voice vote passed 7-0 without dissent.

votes.item_title: Join Social Media Multi-District Litigation and Approve Contingency Fee Retainer Agreement
votes.notes: Litigation against Meta (Facebook/Instagram), ByteDance (TikTok), Snap (Snapchat), and Google (YouTube) represented on contingency by Ward Black Law, Baird Mandalas, and Lieff Cabraser.
votes.discussion_detail: Attorney Janet Ward Black briefed the Board on federal multi-district litigation targeting social media companies Meta, ByteDance, Snap, and Google over youth mental health impacts, explaining the contingency fee retainer carries zero upfront legal cost or financial risk to DPS and preserves individual families' rights to sue separately. Board members Emily Chávez, Natalie Beyer, and Jessica Carda-Auten strongly supported joining the suit both to seek behavior changes and potentially recover unrestricted resources for student mental health support, analogous to Juul settlements. Following consultation with Board Attorney Rod Malone on proper motion wording, Alexandra Valladares moved to join the litigation and approve the retainer agreement, seconded by Jessica Carda-Auten. The motion passed unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Approve Transfer of 2022 General Obligation Bond Funds ($12,421,277) via Durham County Capital Project Ordinance
votes.notes: Disperses $12,421,277 to support priority-order 2022 bond projects (Murray-Massenburg ES, Glenn ES, DSA, Holt ES, Morehead ES).
votes.discussion_detail: Frederick Davis presented the request to transfer $12,421,277 in 2022 General Obligation Bond funds under the County Capital Project Ordinance while reviewing project inflation (30-40%), Murray-Massenburg and Glenn construction progress, and DSA design ahead of summer bidding. Bettina Umstead moved approval (correcting a slip from '2020' to '2022'), seconded by Millicent Rogers. During discussion, Emily Chávez pressed staff on GoDurham bus access and off-site road costs for the new DSA site as well as future uses/appraisals of the existing downtown campus, while Jessica Carda-Auten sought assurances that deferred elementary schools remain safe and retain priority status and Natalie Beyer urged continued energy sustainability design. Following staff responses, the Board passed the bond transfer unanimously 7-0 at 02:43:57.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Work Session | 3/7/24
disagreements.issue: Funding Once-a-Week Elementary World Language Classes vs. Shifting Resources to Dual Language Immersion, EC/ESL Supplements, and CEP
disagreements.summary: During FY 2024-25 budget priority discussions, Vice Chair Emily Chávez argued against investing in once-a-week elementary World Language expansion—contending it benefits non-Latinx students disproportionately—while other members defended World Language equity alongside exploring EC/ESL/bilingual supplements and districtwide CEP.
disagreements.side_a_position: Reconsider costly once-a-week elementary World Language staffing and instead prioritize Dual Language Immersion (DLI), EC/ESL/bilingual staff investments, and outcomes for Black, Latinx, EC, and low-SES students.
side_a_arguments: Once-a-week World Language classes do not create true bilingualism like DLI and may primarily benefit non-Latinx peers.
Resources should center marginalized students—Black, Latinx, EC, and ESL learners—and representation of teachers of color.
disagreements.side_b_position: Maintain neighborhood school World Language equity and Universal Pre-K commitments while simultaneously gathering cost estimates for EC/ESL/bilingual supplements and districtwide CEP.
side_b_arguments: Natalie Beyer noted districtwide CEP and Universal Pre-K belong in county budget asks alongside program evaluations.
Bettina Umstead urged keeping Growing Together equity commitments while requesting concrete cost proposals for EC IAs/certified/classified staff, bilingual stipends, and universal CEP.
disagreements.resolution: Members agreed to await program evaluation data on World Language and DLI while directing administration to bring back cost estimates for EC supplements, bilingual staff stipends, and universal CEP at the next meeting.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 2/22/24
meetings.executive_summary: In Part 1 of the February 22, 2024 monthly meeting (with Jessica Carda-Auten attending virtually), Interim Superintendent Kathy Moore delivered her first regular update and the board heard public comment from classified staff and substitute teachers opposing both the 11% and 15% salary rollback options. The board unanimously approved consent items A through F and adopted 2023-24 Budget Amendment No. 2 (7-0) appropriating $300,000 from fund balance to cover former Superintendent Pascal Mubenga's resignation payout. Board Comptroller Kerry Crutchfield then presented his diagnostic review of the HIL Compensation Study rollout, explaining how compounding 1.5% steps versus legacy 0.85% steps and misordered 4% state raises produced unsustainable deficits, and recommending the 11% interim plan until a permanent market-based schedule can be built for 2024-25. Board members questioned Crutchfield on GAAP reporting, state caps, and the former CFO's siloed contracting before pausing at 02:00:28 to reset stream audio (continuing in Part 2).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Celebrations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead called the February 22, 2024 meeting to order, introduced interpreters Martha Ramirez and Vanessa Pinyette Ramirez, and led a moment of silence. Gina Cooper and Michelle Hayes presented January and February Student, Teacher, and Employee of the Month recognitions, including a $500 DPS Foundation gift card for Student of the Month Chesney and recognition of Employee of the Month Jason Redman.

agenda_items.title: Interim Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Umstead acknowledged Jessica Carda-Auten participating virtually and introduced Interim Superintendent Kathy Moore for her first monthly meeting update. Moore highlighted the DPS arts showcase at the Durham Performing Arts Center featuring over 350 students and ongoing kindergarten readiness outreach for the Class of 2037.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval of January 25, 2024 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board approved the February 22 meeting agenda and the January 25, 2024 regular monthly meeting minutes via voice roll-call votes with no changes.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speakers including classified staff and veteran substitute teachers addressed the board under a one-minute time limit. Commenters opposed both the 11% and 15% salary options for cutting hundreds of dollars from monthly paychecks needed for medication and retirement, urged competitive pay, and criticized perceived financial mismanagement.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A-F)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board approved consent agenda items A through F as reviewed in advance without pulling any items for separate discussion.

agenda_items.title: Operation Services: 2023-24 Budget Amendment No. 2
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Executive Director for Finance Sierra Ojijo presented Budget Amendment No. 2 appropriating $300,000 from local fund balance for the former superintendent's resignation agreement payout. In response to board questions on a prior $700,000 item, audit timing, and rainy-day reserves, Ojijo noted staff were seeking internal budget sources for the $700,000, the external audit remained on track for late March, and while no statutory floor exists, 12% is the standard best practice.

agenda_items.title: Comptroller Update and Salary Implementation Recommendations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board Comptroller Kerry Crutchfield reported that while the HIL study provided useful market data, it lacked an implementation plan and cost estimate, and applying prior 0.85% step years onto 1.5% step schedules before the 4% state raise produced 25-35% increases and an unsustainable deficit. He recommended the 11% interim option over 15% to avoid deepening the deficit while crafting a prospective, market-based 2024-25 plan with 30-day employee notice. Board members questioned him on GAAP reporting, state salary caps, and the former CFO's siloed work with a California consultant before pausing at 02:00:28 for a technical audio reset.

meetings.executive_summary: Resuming after a technical reset, the board completed questioning Comptroller Kerry Crutchfield on the HIL salary study, NC DPI ranges, and state funding caps for English learners and students with disabilities before voting 7-0 to receive his report. Following staff presentations comparing an 11% across-the-board increase ($90.1M, within FY24 budget) against a 15% increase ($2M over budget) and disclosing that maintaining October pay actually cost ~$1M/month including $300K/month for hourly staff, the board voted 5-2 (Chávez and Valladares dissenting) to adopt the 11% Option 1 for March–June 2024 while seeking one-time bridge options for the lowest-paid workers and tasking Crutchfield with permanent FY25 schedules in March. agenda_items.title: Continued Review of Classified Salary Schedule Options (Option 1 Adoption)

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 2/22/24 | Part 2
disagreements.issue: Interim Classified Salary Schedule Option 1 (11% over 2022-23) vs. Honoring October/January Pay or Delaying Implementation
disagreements.summary: The board split 5-2 on adopting Option 1 (restoring 2022-23 salary schedules with an 11% across-the-board increase) for March–June 2024 to stay within the FY24 budget while developing permanent FY25 schedules.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt Option 1 (11% increase with 1-to-1 experience steps) now as the fiscally responsible stopgap within existing FY24 funds while exploring one-time relief for the lowest-paid workers and awaiting permanent FY25 proposals.
side_a_arguments: Honoring October letters costs ~$1M/month ($99M annualized), depleting one-time fund balance and risking future July cuts or ESSER cliff layoffs.
Option 1 restores 1-to-1 public and private experience steps and provides certainty for March–June within budgeted revenue.
All 1,875 classified staff remain at least 11% above 2022-23 pay while Comptroller Crutchfield prepares a permanent market-based FY25 plan.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose immediate implementation of Option 1 and protect workers from pay reductions relative to October/January salary letters without 30 days' notice or granular Group 1 impact data.
side_b_arguments: NC State Personnel Manual Section 4.3 requires at least 30 days' written notice before reducing salary or grade.
68–74% of classified workers (including Group 1 staff earning under $43,450) still face lower pay than October letters, without individualized impact details.
One-time sources or further study during March could avoid abrupt pay reductions before a permanent schedule is ready.
disagreements.resolution: Option 1 passed 5-2 on a roll-call vote (02:07:49), alongside board consensus directing staff to investigate one-time bridge assistance for lowest-paid staff and tasking Crutchfield with returning permanent FY25 options in late March.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Special Meeting | 2/15/24
meetings.executive_summary: In a facilitated special meeting led by former Durham Mayor Steve Schewel, the Board of Education met with Durham Association of Educators (DAE) and NCAE representatives to deliberate on establishing a formal Meet and Confer policy. DAE leaders presented a proposal centered on budget/pay-grade transparency, co-chaired monthly meetings, and organizing-committee accountability, while board members raised questions regarding non-member inclusion—especially after transportation mechanics, fleet maintenance, and lot managers walked out—as well as solicitation rules, superintendent workload, and recent sickouts. After board attorney counsel noted Alexandra Valladares's motion to release the former CFO's November 8 memo was outside the noticed special-meeting agenda, the board voted 6-1 to form a 12-member-plus-alternate ad hoc working group (2 board members + 1 alternate, 2 administrators, 4 DAE members, and 4 non-DAE DPS employees) and unanimously agreed (7-0) to appoint members on February 22.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Approval, and Facilitator Opening
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead called the special meeting with DPS employees and DAE/NCAE representatives to order, introduced interpreters, and the board unanimously approved the agenda. Facilitator Steve Schewel (former Durham Mayor and DPS board member) outlined ground rules emphasizing mutual respect and non-advocacy facilitation.

agenda_items.title: Shared Values and DAE Presentation on Meet and Confer Policy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DAE representatives presented their proposed Meet and Confer framework, highlighting how regular access to state budget-vs-actuals and pay-grade frequency counts would build trust and prevent future payroll crises. They proposed monthly meetings (more frequent in budget season) co-chaired by the DAE president and superintendent, governed through school-level and district organizing committees accountable to workers.

agenda_items.title: Board and DAE Discussion on Inclusion, Representation, and Escalated Actions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members questioned DAE on membership dues, work-hour solicitation, superintendent capacity, school closures from sickouts exhausting instructional make-up days, and non-DAE worker inclusion following a walkout by transportation mechanics and fleet staff. DAE leaders argued their organizing committees engage members and non-members wall-to-wall and that formal co-governance is far more inclusive than informal phone calls. At 03:07:21 Alexandra Valladares moved (seconded by Jovonia Lewis) to release the former CFO's November 8 memo, but board counsel advised the item fell outside the noticed special meeting agenda.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / No vote (Nov 8 memo motion ruled out of agenda scope)

agenda_items.title: Public Comment Opportunity (Transportation & Staff)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Facilitator Schewel invited transportation mechanics, fleet maintenance supervisors, lot managers, and any other attendees wishing to speak to come to the microphone; no speakers came forward after the earlier walkout.

agenda_items.title: Formation, Composition, and Timeline of Meet and Confer Ad Hoc Committee
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After debating Schewel's two-group suggestion and alternative DAE/non-DAE ratios (4-4 vs. 6-2 vs. 5-3), the board voted 6-1 to establish a single ad hoc working group comprising two board members plus one alternate, two administrators, four DAE members, and four non-DAE DPS employees. Following debate with DAE over urgency ahead of March paychecks versus legal review timelines, the board unanimously voted (7-0) for Chair Umstead to appoint members at the February 22 meeting.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Committee composition passed 6-1; Feb 22 appointment timeline passed 7-0

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Special Meeting | 2/15/24
disagreements.issue: Composition and Representation of the Meet and Confer Ad Hoc Working Group
disagreements.summary: Board members and DAE leaders disagreed over whether the Meet and Confer drafting committee should give equal seats to non-union staff (4 DAE / 4 non-DAE) or reflect DAE's union organizing base with a majority or exclusive DAE seat allocation.
disagreements.side_a_position: Include equal employee seats (4 DAE and 4 non-DAE employees alongside 2 administrators and 2 board members + 1 alternate) so all 5,000+ staff have representation.
side_a_arguments: Transportation mechanics, fleet maintenance, and lot managers walked out of the meeting feeling unrepresented by DAE.
An inclusive Durham model should not grant exclusive pay-to-play status to one dues-paying organization over non-members.
Board policy allows the chair to appoint inclusive advisory committees representing diverse job classifications.
disagreements.side_b_position: Grant DAE a majority or exclusive employee seat allocation (e.g., 6 DAE / 2 other, or 8 DAE) rather than an equal 4-4 split with unorganized appointees.
side_b_arguments: DAE drafted the policy, represents roughly 3,000–4,000 workers through democratic organizing committees, and already consults non-members.
Appointing four individual non-DAE employees lacks a democratic accountability structure to a broader worker base.
Carda-Auten floated a 5-3 compromise while Chávez favored 6-2 or 8 DAE to honor DAE's organizing.
disagreements.resolution: The 4 DAE / 4 non-DAE composition passed 6-1 by show of hands (03:24:52), and the board unanimously accelerated member appointments to February 22 (03:37:04).

meetings.executive_summary: Following a 5:00 PM closed session and emotional public comment from classified staff, parents, and elementary student Luna Gomez condemning salary cuts and school closures, the board reviewed four compensation options presented by Dr. Alvera Lesane and CFO Sierra Ojijo—including new 15% options ($93.4M and $94.1M) and data showing February's October-rate payroll cost ~$1M/month ($700K salaried + $300K hourly) as fund balance fell to $6.4M. disagreements.issue: Adopting Option 4 (15% Increase Starting March) Immediately vs. Waiting for Comptroller Analysis and Funding Clarity
disagreements.summary: Following a unanimous vote to maintain October pay rates for February, the board split 3-4 rejecting Jovonia Lewis's motion to adopt Option 4 (15% raise over 2022-23 starting March) and then voted 5-2 to postpone March–June decisions until February 22.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt Option 4 (15% increase with 1-to-1 steps) immediately to end employee anxiety, restore years of experience, and identify ~$2M in one-time funds/fund balance.
side_a_arguments: Leaving employees in limbo damages mental health and risks further school closures and staff departures.
Option 4 honors years of experience at 1-to-1 and ensures every classified employee receives at least 15% over 2022-23.
The ~$2M difference could be covered from fund balance or budget savings while seeking recurring county funds next year.

side_b_arguments: Board lacked complete data on how Option 4 would affect the 567 employees still below October pay, ESSER-funded 113 positions expiring, and declining ADM.
Fund balance had already dropped from ~$11M to $6.4M against a $12.7M target, and staff should not spend unverified funds before comptroller review.
Waiting until February 22 allows administration to model 11%, 12%, and 15% options and share concrete examples with staff.
disagreements.resolution: Option 4 failed 3-4 on roll call (02:48:54), and the board voted 5-2 to postpone March–June compensation decisions to February 22 with board proposals due February 13 (03:04:02).

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Special Meeting | 2/7/24
meetings.executive_summary: In a three-hour special meeting on February 7, 2024, the Board of Education met in closed session for nearly three hours to address attorney-client and confidential personnel matters before returning to open session to announce and unanimously accept Superintendent Pascal Mubenga's resignation (7-0). Chair Bettina Umstead and Board Member Alexandra Valladares read bilingual statements recounting Mubenga's seven-year accomplishments, including COVID-19 recovery, 88% of schools meeting or exceeding growth in 2022-23, and the Bloomberg Philanthropies early college grant. The board also passed a follow-up transitional motion unanimously (7-0) and released a public statement summarizing its attorneys' internal investigation into the payroll crisis—disclosing that the former finance officer knew in February 2023 that pay-raise costs could swing from $10 million to $20 million depending on years-of-service calculations without informing the board, that Mubenga learned on November 8, and that the full board was informed on January 11.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Motion to Enter Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead called the 5:00 PM special meeting to order and the board unanimously approved entering closed session under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3), 143-318.11(a)(6), and 115C-319 for attorney-client privilege and personnel matters, noting a statement would follow.

agenda_items.title: Announcement and Acceptance of Superintendent Pascal Mubenga's Resignation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Returning to open session after closed session, Chair Umstead announced Superintendent Pascal Mubenga's resignation and read a statement (translated into Spanish by Alexandra Valladares) highlighting his seven-year tenure, including two Blue Ribbon schools, 88% of schools meeting/exceeding growth in 2022-23, the multilingual resource center, redistricting, and the Bloomberg grant. The board voted unanimously (7-0) to accept his resignation and approved a subsequent transitional motion (7-0).

agenda_items.title: Public Release of Internal Investigation Summary on Payroll Crisis
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Umstead read the board's statement releasing the attorneys' internal investigation report into the classified pay crisis. The report found that the finance officer knew in February 2023 that pay-raise costs could range from $10M to $20M depending on how years of service were calculated without communicating that variability to the board, that Mubenga first learned of a problem on November 8 and engaged HIL consultants, and that the full board was informed on January 11. Umstead added that the board would meet the next day and had scheduled a meeting with DAE the following week.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3), (a)(6) & 115C-319)
votes.discussion_detail: Entered nearly three-hour closed session for attorney-client privilege and confidential personnel matters.

votes.item_title: Acceptance of Superintendent Pascal Mubenga's Resignation
votes.discussion_detail: Accepted the resignation of Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga following bilingual board remarks recognizing his seven years of service.

votes.notes: Audio transcription at 03:19:40-03:19:57 is partially garbled regarding the exact phrasing of the transitional directive.
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted transitional motion immediately following acceptance of Dr. Mubenga's resignation.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Special Meeting | 2/2/24
meetings.executive_summary: In a nearly eight-hour special meeting on February 2, 2024, the board heard extensive public comment and reviewed staff models showing that full 1-to-1 HIL implementation cost $20M ($9M over budget) while Option 1 (HIL with state experience, $91.2M) and Option 2 (2022-23 schedule + 11% with 1-to-1 steps, $90.1M) fit within FY24 appropriations. After Alexandra Valladares's three motions to unseal personnel records of the CFO and superintendent under NCGS 115C-321(b) died for lack of seconds, the board rejected Option 2 in a 2-5 roll-call vote (Option 1 also failed for lack of a second) and voted 4-3 to table compensation action until February 8. The board then unanimously voted 7-0 to include Valladares's three timeline questions in the pending investigative report, appoint Kerry Crutchfield as independent Board Comptroller (with a conflict-of-interest condition), and direct counsel to terminate HIL consultant contracts, before initiating a vote to schedule a Meet and Confer discussion with DAE and educators, approving an interim CFO personnel report, and concluding with closed session.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review, Addition of Meet and Confer Item, and Initial Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved amending the agenda to add Item 5C (discussion with DAE on Meet and Confer) and moved into closed session for confidential personnel and attorney-client matters until 01:49:25.

agenda_items.title: Compensation Study Options Presentation and General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Alvera Lesane and CFO Sierra Ojijo reported that the $4.5M fund balance transfer reduced reserves from ~$11M to $6.4M (half the recommended level) and presented Option 1 (HIL with state years only, $91.2M) and Option 2 (2022-23 schedule + 11% with 1-to-1 steps, $90.1M), alongside 3-to-1 ($680K FY24) and 2-to-1 external experience models. Chair Umstead noted full 1-to-1 HIL cost $20M ($9M above budget), followed by extended public comment from therapists, classified workers, and parents demanding restoration of verified years of service.

agenda_items.title: Board Deliberation on Compensation Options, Accountability Motions, and Tabling to Feb 8
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members debated hybrid options, legacy ERP/HR software gaps, and transparency. Alexandra Valladares introduced three motions under NCGS 115C-321(b) to disclose when CFO Paul LeSieur, Dr. Mubenga, and board members first knew of the $20M cost discrepancy, all three dying without seconds pending counsel's review of the open investigation. The board rejected Natalie Beyer's motion for Option 2 (2-5), saw Jovonia Lewis's motion for Option 1 die for lack of a second, voted 4-3 to table compensation action to February 8, and unanimously passed Lewis's motion (7-0) ensuring Valladares's three timeline questions are answered in the public investigative report.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Option 2 failed 2-5; Table to Feb 8 passed 4-3; Investigation questions motion passed 7-0

agenda_items.title: Appointment of Board Comptroller and Termination of HIL Contracts
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved appointing Kerry Crutchfield as independent Board Comptroller (with Valladares's friendly amendment barring any prior affiliation with DPS or HIL Group) and unanimously directed board counsel to work with administration to terminate any existing contracts with HIL Consultants as soon as legally permissible.

agenda_items.title: Item 5C: Meet and Confer Discussion with DAE and Educators
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members debated Millicent Rogers's motion to send a doodle poll to schedule an open public conversation with DAE and educators on Meet and Confer, with Valladares pressing for inclusion of non-DAE educators, grassroots groups, and parents, while Rogers and Chávez emphasized starting with the group that brought the proposal in an open public meeting. Roll-call voting began at 05:43:52 before brief audio dropout cut off the tally.

agenda_items.title: Personnel Action (Interim CFO) and Final Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved a personnel report appointing a new interim CFO, heard closing remarks from Chair Umstead centering DPS's 32,000 students and 5,000+ employees, and entered a final closed session from 05:47:10 to 07:46:27 before adjourning.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Special Meeting | 2/2/24
disagreements.issue: Immediate Adoption of Option 2 (11% Schedule) or Option 1 vs. Tabling Compensation Decision to February 8
disagreements.summary: After Option 2 failed 2-5 and Option 1 died without a second, the board split 4-3 to postpone further compensation action until February 8.
disagreements.side_a_position: Table the compensation decision to February 8 (after rejecting Option 2) so staff and the newly appointed comptroller can provide additional fiscal clarity and avoid rushing into an unpopular cut.
side_a_arguments: Board members felt pressured without full financial health data and wanted time to collaborate with staff, DAE, and the new comptroller.
Payroll could still accommodate a February 8 decision if made early enough.
disagreements.side_b_position: Make an immediate decision on February 2 (supporting Option 1 or opposing further delay) so employees have certainty and are not left in limbo.
side_b_arguments: Delaying another week 'kicks the can down the road' and prolongs employee anxiety and potential school walkouts.
Staff had already provided budgeted options (Option 1 at $91.2M or Option 2 at $90.1M) enabling a timely decision.
disagreements.resolution: Option 2 failed 2-5 (04:43:11) and the motion to table until February 8 carried 4-3 (04:47:36).

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Special Meeting | 2/2/24
disagreements.issue: Scope of Meet and Confer Engagement: DAE-Led vs. Broad Cross-Section of Educators and Parents
disagreements.summary: Board members debated whether the proposed Meet and Confer conversation should start specifically with DAE leadership or explicitly encompass non-DAE advocacy groups, non-union educators, and parents.
disagreements.side_a_position: Invite a broad cross-section of current DPS educators, PTAs, parent advocates, and multiple groups alongside DAE to avoid giving exclusive preference to one dues-charging organization.
side_a_arguments: Not all DPS employees belong to DAE, and parents/PTAs and non-union groups are also impacted by district decisions.
Starting on the right foot requires avoiding 'pay-to-play' perception and external organizers.
disagreements.side_b_position: Begin the initial public conversation with DAE leadership—who brought the Meet and Confer proposal—while keeping the meeting open to the public and discussing broader inclusion together.
side_b_arguments: DAE brought the policy proposal and represents thousands of DPS workers.
Every board meeting is public by law, and the group can determine broader participation rules once convened.
disagreements.resolution: Board initiated a roll-call vote at 05:43:52 on Rogers's motion to send a doodle poll for an open meeting with DAE leadership (audio cut out before final tally, though the meeting subsequently occurred on Feb 15).

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 1/25/24
meetings.executive_summary: At its January 25, 2024 monthly meeting—preceded by a two-hour closed session—the Board of Education apologized to employees for the classified salary schedule crisis and waived Board Policy 2330 (7-0) to add emergency budget and compensation actions to the agenda. Following intense public comment from therapists, instructional assistants, and classified staff protesting the retroactive removal of verified experience steps, Senior Executive Director for Finance Sierra Ojijo presented FY 2023-24 Budget Amendment No. 1 appropriating $4,539,435 from unassigned fund balance (leaving ~$6.41M) to cover July–January overages. The board unanimously approved the amendment (7-0), ratified all October 2023-notified salary payments through January 31, 2024 while barring any repayment clawbacks (7-0), and directed Central Services to guarantee every affected classified employee earns no less than their 2022-23 pay and at least a 4% monthly increase starting in February (7-0). The board also waived second reading to cut purchasing and construction approval thresholds back to $90,000 (7-0), passed Mentoring and MLK resolutions, approved the personnel report and a special education contract, and scheduled a February 2 special meeting after a second closed session.

agenda_items.title: 5:00 PM Special Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead opened the 5:00 PM special session and the board unanimously entered closed session under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(1), (a)(3), and (a)(6) for personnel and attorney-client matters until 02:24:00.

agenda_items.title: Open Session Call to Order, Chair Apology, and Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Umstead apologized for the salary schedule harm and broken trust, pledging concrete corrective actions. Superintendent Pascal Mubenga assured employees of a resolution, thanked the board for School Board Appreciation Month, and celebrated the Bloomberg Philanthropies grant partnership with Durham Tech and Duke Health.

agenda_items.title: Waiver of Policy 2330, Agenda Amendment, and December 14, 2023 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously waived Board Policy 2330 to allow unposted budget action items, amended the agenda to add Budget Amendment No. 1 (Item 8A) and Classified Staff Compensation (Item 8B), and approved the December 14, 2023 meeting minutes.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Physical therapists, occupational therapists, classified employees, parents, and community members spoke under a one-minute limit. Speakers condemned the revocation of previously verified years of experience (such as dropping from step 33 to step 1 or step 8 to step 0) and demanded no clawbacks and full transparency.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved the January 25 consent agenda without pulling any items.

agenda_items.title: Items 8A & 8B: FY24 Budget Amendment No. 1 and Classified Compensation Safeguards
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance Director Sierra Ojijo presented Budget Amendment No. 1 transferring $4,539,435 from unassigned local fund balance (out of $10.9M unassigned / $16M total) to cover July 2023–January 2024 classified salary overages, leaving ~$6.41M. The board unanimously approved the amendment (7-0), ratified October-notified salary payments through January 31, 2024 while directing Central Services not to seek repayment (7-0), and passed Jovonia Lewis's motion guaranteeing no employee earns below their 2022-23 monthly rate and all remaining staff receive at least a 4% increase beginning February 2024 (7-0).
agenda_items.vote_summary: Budget Amendment 1 passed 7-0; Ratification/no-repayment 7-0; 4% floor & hold-harmless 7-0

agenda_items.title: National Mentoring Month Proclamation & Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After a recess, board members read and unanimously adopted the National Mentoring Month Proclamation emphasizing critical mentoring for youth of color, followed by the resolution honoring Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Day.

agenda_items.title: Purchasing and Construction Policy Amendments (Reduction to $90,000 Threshold)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of Staff Dr. Tanya Giovanni reviewed prior board changes to purchasing and construction thresholds (raised from $90K to $200K in August 2022 and lowered to $150K/$400K in September 2023). Emphasizing fiduciary oversight, the board unanimously waived second reading and amended Policies 6420, 6430, 6450, 9030, 9110, and 9120 to lower all thresholds back to $90,000.

agenda_items.title: Closed Sessions, Personnel Report, EC Placement Agreement, and Feb 2 Scheduling
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board entered closed session at 04:57:52, returned at 05:29:57 to unanimously approve the January 25 personnel report and a special education placement agreement, and voted to enter a second closed session until 07:45:26 before scheduling a special meeting for Friday, February 2 at 3:00 PM and adjourning.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 1/11/24
meetings.executive_summary: At its January 11, 2024 work session, the Board of Education unanimously approved the agenda, the November 2, 2023 minutes, and a consent item upgrading K-5 math curriculum resources to Eureka Math Squared (7-0). Academic Services presented the final five-year review of the 2018-2023 Strategic Plan—highlighting 88.2% of schools meeting or exceeding growth (first among peer districts), improved substitute fill rates (~70%), and >95% attendance alongside post-pandemic challenges in proficiency and suspensions. Dr. King then delivered the baseline report for the Black and Hispanic Student Achievement Plan across nine statements of intention aligned with 2023-2028 Strategic Plan Goals 1 and 2, prompting board discussion on advisory council design, chronic absenteeism, EC equity dashboards, and SB 49's impact on climate surveys, and a unanimous vote (7-0) to amend the baseline resolution record to reflect DPS's prior ESL/LEP resolution. Following a closed session from 02:53:41 to 05:28:19, the board approved the amended January 11 personnel report (7-0) and announced a $315,000 insurance-paid legal settlement.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Approval, and November 2, 2023 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead called the January 11, 2024 work session to order, thanked staff for navigating severe weather, and led a moment of silence. The board unanimously approved the agenda and the November 2, 2023 work session minutes; no speakers signed up for general public comment.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda: Upgrade to Eureka Math Squared K-5 Curriculum
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved the single consent item upgrading K-5 mathematics curriculum resources to Eureka Math Squared.

agenda_items.title: Academic Services: Final Update on 2018-2023 Strategic Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Pittman, Dr. Alvera Lesane, and priority champions presented final five-year longitudinal outcomes across all five strategic plan pillars, noting 88.2% of schools met or exceeded growth (1st among peer districts), 84.3% graduation gains, 100% adoption of social-emotional cultural frameworks, substitute fill rates rising from <50% to ~70%, Hispanic/Latino hiring reaching 8.15%, and >95% attendance. Board members discussed rising post-pandemic out-of-school suspensions above the 4% target, restorative practices, and student mentorship.

agenda_items.title: Black and Hispanic Student Achievement Plan Baseline Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. King presented the baseline report for the Black and Hispanic Student Achievement Plan anchored in nine statements of intention under 2023-2028 Strategic Plan Goals 1 and 2, covering academic growth, grade-level proficiency gaps (>30 points for Black/Hispanic and ~50 points for SWD/LEP), graduation rates (76.8% Hispanic, 86% Black), ACT WorkKeys, ELL progress, EC growth (20% of 34 schools), suspensions (13.54% Black vs. 5% goal), attendance, climate surveys (down 30-60% under SB 49), and $240,304 in school-reported targeted funding. Board members discussed chronic absenteeism, EC equity dashboards, EL learning coaches, and unanimously passed Alexandra Valladares's motion amending the resolution record to reference the prior ESL/LEP student support resolution.

agenda_items.title: Follow-Up Summary, Closed Session, Personnel Report, and Legal Settlement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board and staff summarized follow-up items (restorative practice resources, advisory council structure, EL suspension data, and EC equity dashboard) before entering closed session at 02:53:41. Returning at 05:28:19, the board unanimously approved the amended January 11 personnel report (7-0) and Counsel Rob Malone announced a $315,000 settlement paid by the board's insurance carrier in E.S. by Guardian ad Litem K.S. v. Durham Public Schools Board of Education et al.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 12/14/23
meetings.executive_summary: At its final monthly meeting of 2023, the DPS Board of Education approved the FY 2023-24 Budget Resolution unanimously (7-0) following CFO Paul LeSieur's presentation detailing a 56% state / 36.3% local / 7.9% federal revenue mix, $72 million in federal COVID funds to be spent by September 30, 2024, over 5,037 full-time positions, and recent $1,500 ESSER II and $500 staff bonuses. Board members also deferred a resolution on the Black and Hispanic Achievement Plan to the January work session (7-0) so departing inaugural Equity Director Dr. Kelvin Bullock could deliver his final LGBTQIA+ Task Force update on state legislative impacts and a student safety infographic. Earlier in the meeting, 22 public commenters addressed topics including support for queer students and staff and the new Durham School of the Arts plan. After a closed session expanded under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(8) to formulate school safety plans, the board approved the December 14 personnel report by a 6-1 voice vote and unanimously approved the school system safety plans (7-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Celebrations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead called the meeting to order, introduced interpreters Marty Ramirez and Vanessa Peña Ramirez, and held a moment of silence. Shina Cooper led December celebrations honoring Student of the Month Layla (Riverside High School, presented by PLTW teacher Seth Stallings), Teacher of the Month Joy Mason (Montessori educator and Rainbow Club advisor), Employee of the Month, Spark Pin recipient Sherrod Washington (DPS Transportation bus driver), and departing inaugural Equity Director Dr. Kelvin Bullock.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga highlighted the November 18 DPS Annual Showcase of Schools at the Durham Convention Center and ongoing school tours through January. He also noted recognition from NCDPI's Office of Advanced Learning and Gifted Education for expanding advanced course access and thanked Assistant Superintendent Dr. Dan Davis for six years of service.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval of November 16, 2023 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board approved the December 14 meeting agenda (moved by Natalie Beyer, seconded by Jovonia Lewis) and the November 16, 2023 monthly meeting minutes (moved by Natalie Beyer, seconded by Millicent Rogers) without modification.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Twenty-two speakers signed up to address the board under a two-minute time limit. Opening remarks by a school GSA advisor urged continued support for queer staff and students via the LGBTQIA+ task force, careful vetting of professional development speakers, and attention to the new Durham School of the Arts plan.

agenda_items.title: FY 2023-24 Budget Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Paul LeSieur presented the FY 2023-24 budget resolution, noting a delayed state budget with a $2,000 beginning teacher pay bump ($37,000 to $39,000) and ~4% average increase, $1,500 ESSER II and $500 bonuses, an estimated $10.95 million fund balance (with $1.5 million appropriated), $72 million in remaining federal COVID funds, and over 5,037 full-time positions. Salaries and benefits accounted for over 78% of non-capital spending ($391 million in school-based/instructional support alongside $213 million in capital improvements); board members criticized the state's 10.6% funding cap on ESL and students-with-disabilities allotments before voting unanimously to adopt the resolution.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Given the late hour, the board voted 7-0 to defer the Black and Hispanic Achievement Plan resolution to the January work session so Dr. Kelvin Bullock could present before his departure. Dr. Bullock then delivered an update on the LGBTQIA+ Task Force, reviewing state and federal legislative impacts and a draft student safety infographic prepared with Dr. Tanya Giovanni's team.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 11/16/23
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 16, 2023 monthly meeting, the DPS Board of Education unanimously removed Policies 3540, 1735, and 1310 (related to SB 49) from the agenda for further work following public comments reflecting sharp community division over parental notification and LGBTQIA+ student protections. The central contested vote was a 5-2 approval to purchase 4,002 replacement Chromebooks from CDW-G, with Millicent Rogers and Jessica Carda-Auten dissenting amid board debate over 1,221 unrecovered devices assigned to former students, incentive-based device recovery, Pre-K–2 appropriateness, and an upcoming ESSER funding cliff for 11 IT technician positions. The board also recognized November honorees including Hillside High IB senior Santiago Parejo and Forest View Elementary teacher Lily McCormick, unanimously approved October 26 minutes, and approved the November 16 personnel report 7-0 after closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Celebrations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead called the meeting to order and led a moment of silence. Shina Cooper presented November recognitions including Student of the Month Santiago Parejo (Hillside High School IB senior, presented by Principal Dr. William Logan), Pearsontown Elementary's state-leader recognition, Teacher of the Month Lily McCormick (second grade, Forest View Elementary), Employee of the Month, and Spark Pins including Durham County Sheriff's deputies supporting students.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga highlighted the district's first Wellness Day held October 27—featuring Zumba, yoga, character development, and affirmations coordinated by Student Services—and expressed gratitude to DPS employees, students, and families in his seventh year.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Amendment (Removing Policies 3540, 1735, and 1310) and October 26 Minutes Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With Emily Chávez participating virtually, Millicent Rogers moved and Natalie Beyer seconded amending the agenda to remove Policies 3540, 1735, and 1310 so the board could continue working on them; the amended agenda passed by voice vote. The board then unanimously approved the October 26, 2023 monthly meeting minutes (7-0).

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public speakers included a presenter requesting permission to erect a historical plaque at the former Durham High School building (following a 2018 board proposal) and commenters sharply divided over SB 49 and Policy 1310. One speaker thanked the board for pausing SB 49 policy revisions to prevent harm to students, while another urged the board not to stand between parents and children on biological sex.

agenda_items.title: One-to-One Chromebook Sustainability Update and Purchase of 4,002 Chromebooks from CDW-G
agenda_items.discussion_summary: IT staff reported on Phase 2 staff device deployment, 1,221 Chromebooks still assigned to students no longer enrolled in DPS, a ~5% peer-district loss rate, and limited state funding (~$300,000 plus fines/forfeitures for equipment, zero for IT staff) as 11 ESSER-funded technician positions approach a federal funding cliff. Board members debated whether to continue a districtwide 1:1 model (especially for Pre-K–2), parent visibility into assignment logs, and offering incentives to recover unreturned devices before voting 5-2 to approve buying 4,002 Chromebooks from CDW-G.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 11/16/23
disagreements.issue: Purchase of 4,002 Chromebooks from CDW-G and 1:1 Device Sustainability
disagreements.summary: The board split 5-2 on approving a purchase of 4,002 replacement Chromebooks from CDW-G amid questions over unrecovered devices, recovery incentives, and long-term sustainability once federal ESSER funds expire.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the 4,002 Chromebook purchase now to replace damaged devices in students' hands while continuing to evaluate long-term 1:1 sustainability.
side_a_arguments: Replacement devices are needed immediately to swap out broken or damaged student Chromebooks while harvesting salvageable parts.
District loss rates align with peer districts (~5%) and administration can return with budget sustainability recommendations.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose the Chromebook purchase pending stronger device recovery accountability, parent portal transparency, and budget/program clarity.
side_b_arguments: 1,221 devices remain assigned to students no longer enrolled in DPS, and families lack online visibility into which devices were issued to their children.
Spending budget dollars on recovery incentives ('bribing back' devices) before exhausting direct recovery requests is concerning.
disagreements.resolution: Motion to purchase 4,002 Chromebooks from CDW-G passed 5-2; staff committed to bringing back long-term 1:1 sustainability recommendations.
