meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Public Hearing for Policy 1310 | 11/9/23
meetings.executive_summary: This special public hearing gathered community feedback on draft revisions to Policy 1310 (Parental Engagement) prompted by North Carolina Senate Bill 49 (the Parents' Bill of Rights), following the board's November 2 announcement. Facilitated with DPS administration with a three-minute limit per speaker and open until 6:30 PM, the hearing featured no board motions or votes. Speakers supporting strict SB 49 compliance (including Grant Berry, Ingrid Connolly, and Sky Sanchez) criticized vague wording, marketing data opt-out provisions, missing healthcare consent language for Hillside High School's clinic, short-duration counseling exceptions, and K-4 student-initiated question exceptions on gender identity. Conversely, parents, graduates, and LGBTQIA+ advocates (including Kate Delander, Luca, and Laudana Bets) urged the board to resist or slow compliance with SB 49, protect DPS's existing gender support policy, warn students before outing them to parents, and shield elementary classrooms and teachers from restrictive rules.

agenda_items.title: Opening Remarks and Public Hearing Rules for Policy 1310
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The facilitator welcomed in-person, Zoom, and livestream participants to the Policy 1310 (Parental Engagement) public comment hearing requested by the board on November 2. Speakers were allotted three minutes each, instructed not to name staff, students, or parents in complaints, and advised that DPS administration and board members would listen without engaging in discussion.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment on Draft Policy 1310 and SB 49 Compliance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Registered speakers presented sharply contrasting perspectives on Policy 1310. Grant Berry, Ingrid Connolly, Sky Sanchez, and an Orange County resident argued the draft deviated from SB 49 (N.C.G.S. 115C-76.25 / 76.75) via vague language, marketing survey opt-outs, omitted Hillside High clinic treatment consent, discipline-related counseling carve-outs, and K-4 instruction exceptions; conversely, Kate Delander, Luca, Laudana Bets (citing Parker v. Hurley), and another speaker urged resisting forced student outing, protecting trans and gender-diverse youth, and preserving DPS's gender support policy.

agenda_items.title: Session Hold Until 6:30 PM and Written Feedback Instructions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After registered speakers concluded, officials announced the hearing would remain open until the scheduled 6:30 PM end time to accommodate late arrivals and reminded community members that written comments could be submitted to policy1310@dpsnc.net.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Public Hearing for Policy 1310 | 11/9/23
disagreements.issue: Draft Policy 1310 (Parental Engagement) Alignment with SB 49 vs. LGBTQIA+ Student Protections
disagreements.summary: Public hearing speakers split sharply over whether Draft Policy 1310 went too far in accommodating classroom discussions and opt-out exceptions relative to SB 49 or went too far in complying with state mandates that require parental pronoun notifications and restrict K-4 gender/sexuality instruction.
disagreements.side_a_position: Align Policy 1310 strictly and clearly with all SB 49 (Parents' Bill of Rights) statutory mandates.
side_a_arguments: SB 49 applies statewide across all 100 counties regardless of local opposition.

Draft Policy 1310 omits explicit parental consent rules for healthcare clinics (e.g., Hillside High), allows marketing/opt-out and short-duration counseling exceptions, uses vague 'responsible parenting' phrasing, and permits K-4 gender discussions via student-initiated questions.
disagreements.side_b_position: Resist, delay, or narrow Policy 1310 changes to uphold DPS's gender support policy and protect LGBTQIA+ students and educators.
side_b_arguments: Requiring staff to notify parents of pronoun/name changes outs vulnerable students and erodes trust with educators.

Restricting K-4 classroom discussions marginalizes trans kindergartners and families with same-sex parents, while Parker v. Hurley precedent rejects claims that inclusive curriculum burdens parental rights.
disagreements.resolution: Public hearing for feedback only; no board action taken at this session.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 11/2/23
meetings.executive_summary: Convening in a November 2 work session led by Millicent Rogers (with Board Chair Bettina Umstead presiding after closed session), the board focused heavily on six policy revisions prompted by North Carolina Senate Bill 49 (the Parents' Bill of Rights), including Policies 4002 and 4335, while scheduling formal public engagement for Policy 1310. Five public commenters—including Public School Strong, Rainbow Collective for Change, and a DPS educator/parent—urged the board to protect LGBTQIA+ youth and refuse or delay SB 49 compliance. Although board members expressed strong opposition to SB 49's K-4 restrictions and parental pronoun-notification mandates, legal counsel warned that state law applies regardless of local policy and that abstentions count as 'yes' votes without a conflict of interest; the board voted unanimously (6-0) to bring the six policies back for second reading on November 16 alongside staff guidance and training timelines. Following closed session, all seven members unanimously approved (7-0) the November 2 personnel report and a contract addendum following Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga's evaluation.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Approval, and October 12, 2023 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The work session opened with Jovonia Lewis participating remotely and Alexandra Valladares initially absent. The board approved the agenda 6-0 on roll call (moved by Bettina Umstead, seconded by Natalie Beyer) and approved the October 12, 2023 work session minutes 6-0 on roll call (moved by Emily Chávez, seconded by Jessica Carda-Auten).

agenda_items.title: Public Comment on SB 49 and DPS LGBTQIA+ Policy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Five speakers addressed SB 49 and proposed DPS policy changes. Representatives of Public School Strong, Rainbow Collective for Change, and Sandy Ridge staff/parents urged the board to stand by DPS's existing LGBTQIA+ and Gender Support Policy, clarify accountability for staff over-compliance, delay policy changes until January or court resolution, or refuse to comply altogether.

agenda_items.title: First Reading of Six SB 49-Aligned Policies (Including Policy 4002 & 4335) and Policy 1310 Engagement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and legal counsel Mr. Malone presented six SB 49-related policy updates on first reading (noting student-initiated question exceptions in Policy 4002 and criminal reporting in Policy 4335) and outlined statutory community engagement required for Policy 1310. Board members Emily Chávez, Jessica Carda-Auten, Natalie Beyer, and Bettina Umstead condemned SB 49's K-4 restrictions and forced student-outing provisions while debating whether staff guidance should precede policy adoption and whether members could abstain, ultimately voting unanimously to advance the six policies to a November 16 second reading.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed Unanimously (advance to second reading on Nov 16)

agenda_items.title: Summary of Follow-Up Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The presiding member summarized board directives: return the six policies for second reading on November 16, have Dr. Tanya Giovanni and legal counsel Mr. Malone finalize staff procedures and training timelines by November 16, post Policy 1310 online for feedback, and invite the LGBTQIA+ Task Force to the upcoming public hearing.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session, November 2 Personnel Report, and Superintendent Evaluation Contract Addendum
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board entered closed session unanimously by roll call at 01:17:39. Reconvening in open session at 03:20:50 with Chair Bettina Umstead presiding and all seven members present, the board unanimously approved the November 2 personnel report (7-0) and praised Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga's leadership before approving a contract addendum unanimously (7-0).

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 11/2/23
disagreements.issue: Navigating SB 49 Policy Updates vs. Non-Compliance and Staff Guidance Timing
disagreements.summary: While board members unanimously advanced six SB 49-aligned policies to a second reading, the discussion exposed sharp tensions over complying with a state law members viewed as harmful, whether staff guidance should precede policy adoption, and public demands for outright non-compliance.
disagreements.side_a_position: Delay or refuse policy changes until January or until staff procedures and protections are ready, avoiding endorsement of harmful state mandates.
side_a_arguments: Public commenters urged DPS to defy SB 49 and keep existing LGBTQIA+ protections intact.

Jessica Carda-Auten expressed reluctance to amend policies before or without simultaneous administrative guidance for teachers, and Emily Chávez criticized SB 49's K-4 restrictions and forced student outing.
disagreements.side_b_position: Advance the policy revisions and adopt accompanying administrative procedures so staff are not left in legal jeopardy or an ambiguous 'no man's land'.
side_b_arguments: Counsel Mr. Malone advised that SB 49's instructional and notice rules are already state law regardless of local board policy, and asking staff to break the law risks harming employees.
Staff noted formal procedures cannot be issued until the board adopts the underlying policies, and without clear procedures individual schools could act inconsistently.
disagreements.resolution: Board voted unanimously to bring the six policies back for second reading on November 16 while directing staff to prepare accompanying procedures and training timelines by that date.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 8/24/23
meetings.executive_summary: With Jessica Carda-Auten absent, the DPS Board of Education opened its August 24, 2023 monthly meeting with an official statement read by Chair Bettina Umstead condemning the NC General Assembly's recent veto overrides of three bills targeting trans and gender-diverse youth and pledging continued support for LGBTQIA+ students. Celebrations highlighted DPS Foundation sponsorships and the Rising Stars summer internship program doubling from 22 to over 44 student interns, while Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga announced traditional schools opening August 28, the rescheduled August 31 opening of the new Northern High School, $200 staff payments, and the September 21 final-beam ceremony for Murray-Massenburg Elementary. The board unanimously removed Item 6 (minutes) from the agenda (6-0) and heard public commenters including high school students opposing Smart Lunch schedule changes. In an extensive policy review, board members directed staff to prepare a September second reading raising the board contract-approval threshold above $90,000 and tracking cumulative per-vendor awards, before unanimously entering closed session and approving the August 24 personnel report (6-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Board Statement on NC General Assembly Veto Overrides, and Moment of Silence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead called the meeting to order and read a Board of Education statement expressing disappointment over the General Assembly's override of Governor Cooper's vetoes on six bills—three targeting trans and gender-diverse youth—while affirming DPS's commitment to LGBTQIA+ students and noting staff were reviewing the new laws before issuing guidance.

agenda_items.title: Celebrations: DPS Foundation, Rising Stars Internships, and Spark Pins
agenda_items.discussion_summary: New Executive Director of Communications Shina Cooper recognized DPS Foundation sponsorships (including the new Student of the Month program) and introduced Workforce Development Coordinator Jamia Jones, who celebrated the Rising Stars CTE internship program doubling from 22 interns in 2022 to over 44 in 2023 across partners including Durham Water Management, Merck, GSK, and Duke Facilities. Spark Pins were presented to Mr. Williamson and Ralph Ransom's maintenance team.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga reported traditional schools would open August 28, noted the opening of the new Northern High School was rescheduled to Thursday, August 31, highlighted $200 payments going out to remaining staff, and announced a September 21 final-beam ceremony for the new Murray-Massenburg Elementary School.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review (Removing Item 6 Minutes) and General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Noting Jessica Carda-Auten's absence, the board voted 6-0 to remove Item 6 (monthly minutes) from the agenda and 6-0 to adopt the amended agenda. Public speakers included Ann Reebick (Public School Strong) and a student objecting to a principal's proposal to alter Smart Lunch tutoring and club periods.

agenda_items.title: Procurement and Contract Approval Threshold Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff briefed the board on contracts below the $90,000 board-approval threshold—including contracted nurses/EC services, consultants, and principal-level contracts up to $10,000 (reported twice yearly). Board members debated strict threshold adherence versus discretionary escalation of near-cap contracts, and Chair Umstead summarized consensus for staff to return in September with a second reading raising the threshold and capturing cumulative vendor totals above it, alongside reviewing grounds/custodial capacity for new campuses.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 8/10/23
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Chair Jovonia Lewis with Natalie Beyer participating virtually and Jessica Carda-Auten arriving after initial procedural votes, the board held an extended work session reviewing equity, personnel policies, and finances. Board members engaged in an extended debate over a draft Black and Hispanic Student Achievement Plan resolution (Item 7A), ultimately agreeing to collaborate with Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga and staff to align its metrics and Family Advisory Council timeline with the Strategic Plan for the September work session. On first reading, the board reviewed Policy 7503 (Teleworking) and Policy 1710 (Prohibition Against Discrimination, Harassment, and Bullying), declining to waive second reading on Policy 1710 so staff could address protected-class language and same-gender Title IX contact options by August 24. The board unanimously approved (7-0) allocating $20 per 20th-day enrolled student (~$625,000) for school-level student and staff incentives with new equity guidance, heard a Q4 ESSER update showing roughly $70 million (46%) remaining across ESSER II and III, and after closed session approved the August 10 personnel report 5-1 with Beyer absent.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jovonia Lewis called the August 10, 2023 work session to order, recognized Spanish interpreters Martha Romo-Eguiles and Marty Ramirez, and led a moment of silence. On roll call for agenda approval with Natalie Beyer participating virtually and Jessica Carda-Auten not yet present, Millicent Rogers voted no because she had not yet been given a chance to ask about tabling Item 7A, though the motion carried 5-1.

agenda_items.title: Approval of May 4, 2023 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members reviewed the minutes of the May 4, 2023 monthly work session with no corrections requested. Millicent Rogers moved approval and Natalie Beyer seconded.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Three public speakers addressed the board. Nicholas Graber-Grace thanked Chief of Staff Tanya Giovanni for Riverside Smart Lunch safety data and urged DPS to pursue federal Inflation Reduction Act green energy and construction grants, while a primary Montessori teacher warned that requiring general-education Montessori teachers to serve as Exceptional Children (EC) case managers without BK/EC-certified staffing created legal and instructional strain.

agenda_items.title: Consent Items (6A-6D)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Lewis noted consent items 6A through 6D had been reviewed ahead of the work session. Bettina Umstead moved approval and Emily Chávez seconded with no items pulled for discussion.

agenda_items.title: Board of Education Item 7A: Black and Hispanic Student Achievement Plan Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Millicent Rogers, Natalie Beyer, and Jessica Carda-Auten introduced a draft resolution establishing a Black and Hispanic Student Achievement Plan with quarterly reporting and a Family Advisory Council. Board members and Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga debated avoiding redundancy with the 2023-2028 Strategic Plan, ensuring immigrant/English-learner inclusion, realistic December 2023 timelines, and predictive vs. annual testing metrics, reaching consensus for Rogers and another board member to refine the draft with staff for September.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / No vote (deferred to September work session)

agenda_items.title: Chief of Staff: Policy 7503 (Teleworking) - First Reading
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of Staff Dr. Tanya Giovanni presented Policy 7503 on first reading to formalize discretionary, hybrid (2-3 days/week), and hard-to-fill full-time telework options (such as IT) while keeping DPS worksites as the default. Board members praised caregiving flexibility and asked staff to clarify out-of-state and out-of-country legal/tax compliance and HR equity review procedures before returning on August 24.

agenda_items.title: Chief of Staff: Policy 1710 (Prohibition Against Discrimination, Harassment, and Bullying) - First Reading
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Giovanni proposed updating Policy 1710 to add sexual orientation and gender identity as protected classes, adopt gender-neutral pronouns, cross-reference the LGBTQIA+ gender supports policy, split Title IX coordination between Karen Beckett (students) and Jeff Koweek (employees), and name Dr. Melissa Watson as Section 504 coordinator. After members questioned adding religion and language upfront, naming individuals vs. titles, and guaranteeing same-gender Title IX contact options, administration withdrew its request to waive second reading so revisions could return August 24.

agenda_items.title: Operation Services Item 9A: Per-Pupil School Incentive Funding ($20 per Student)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance staff requested ~$625,000 ($20 per 20th-day ADM student) for school-level student and staff incentives paired with new Office of Equity and Professional Development guidance requiring School Improvement Team (SIT) and principal-supervisor approval. While Millicent Rogers urged a per-student dollar cap after past $300/Xbox awards, Chair Lewis and Natalie Beyer cautioned against micromanaging SITs and the board approved the allocation 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Operation Services: ESSER Funding Update (SY 2022-23 Q4) and Introduction of COO Larry Johnson
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Paul LeSieur reported roughly 46% (~$70 million) remaining across ESSER II ($7.9M remaining, set to close out September 30, 2023 via September 15 staff bonuses) and ESSER III ($62M remaining of $109M, due September 2024), warning that expiring 109 temporary school positions (~$7M/year) and expanding CEP from 17 to 29 schools (reducing Title I allocations by ~$2M) would create FY 2024-25 budget pressures. Chair Lewis and Dr. Mubenga also welcomed newly hired Chief Operating Officer Larry Johnson.

agenda_items.title: Summary Follow-Up, Closed Session, and Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Stewart summarized follow-up items for the August 24 and September meetings before the board voted 6-0 to enter closed session. Reconvening in open session at 03:28:51 with Natalie Beyer no longer present, the board approved the August 10, 2023 personnel report by a 5-1 voice vote and adjourned.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 8/10/23
disagreements.issue: Design, Metrics, and Timeline for Black and Hispanic Student Achievement Plan Resolution
disagreements.summary: Board members and Superintendent Dr. Mubenga differed over adopting the draft Black and Hispanic Student Achievement resolution as written versus refining its alignment with the Strategic Plan, Family Advisory Council structure, and realistic reporting cadence.
disagreements.side_a_position: Move forward urgently with an explicit resolution, frequent deliverables, and a dedicated Family Advisory Council focused on Black and Hispanic students.
side_a_arguments: Black and Hispanic students make up roughly 80% of DPS and require urgent, explicit accountability beyond general strategic plan language.
An explicit Family Advisory Council and more frequent deliverables will strengthen community trust and oversight.
disagreements.side_b_position: Take several weeks to align metrics with annual data availability, incorporate existing parent advisory structures and ESL/immigrant language, and ensure realistic timelines.
side_b_arguments: Annual state assessment metrics cannot change meaningfully on a quarterly cadence, and December 2023 turnaround is too compressed for authentic council recruitment.
The resolution should explicitly align with Strategic Plan Goals 1B, 2B, and 3C and acknowledge immigrant/ESL students without duplicating staff workload.
disagreements.resolution: No vote taken; board reached consensus for Millicent Rogers and a colleague to work with Superintendent Mubenga's team on a revised draft for the September work session.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 8/10/23
disagreements.issue: Whether to Impose a Hard Per-Student Dollar Cap on School Incentive Funds
disagreements.summary: Board members disagreed on whether the $20-per-student school funding allocation should include a strict dollar ceiling per award or rely on School Improvement Teams and equity guidance.
disagreements.side_a_position: Establish explicit per-student dollar limits on student incentive awards comparable to teacher appreciation gift limits.
side_a_arguments: Past high-dollar items such as $300 awards, expensive jackets, or gaming consoles create inequities with staff gift limits and difficult family situations.
disagreements.side_b_position: Rely on the new Office of Equity and Professional Development guidance plus SIT and principal-supervisor review rather than rigid spending caps.
side_b_arguments: Rigid caps could overly restrict school improvement teams from funding meaningful group incentives and educational field trips.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 7-0 without a formal dollar cap, with staff asked to clarify field-trip guidelines and consider earlier June approval for year-round schools.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 6/15/23
meetings.executive_summary: With six members present (Emily Chávez absent and Jovonia Lewis joining virtually), the board took decisive votes on major capital, safety, and student assignment policies. Members unanimously adopted resolutions recognizing June as LGBTQ+ Pride Month, urging the NC General Assembly to invest in >=18% teacher pay raises and halt private school voucher expansion, and approving a $57.05 million Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) renovation and addition contract for Glenn Elementary School (26.9% MWBE). The board split 4-2 to renew the 22-SRO contract with the Durham County Sheriff's Office for 2023-24 while awaiting the Community Safety and Wellness Task Force's October recommendations, and split 4-2 again to adopt the Growing Together secondary boundary and program plan, converting School for Creative Studies from a 6-12 campus into a 6-8 year-round middle school over objections from Millicent Rogers and Alexandra Valladares.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Celebrations, and Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead convened the June 15 meeting and recognized retiring senior leaders Chip Sudderth and Dr. Hardy. Celebrations honored Riverside High School engineering educator Seth Stylings (2023 NCAT CTE Teacher of the Year, who urged continued advocacy on teacher salaries and affordable housing) and presented the NC PTA Distinguished Service Award to DPS, followed by Superintendent Dr. Mabenga highlighting ~$70 million in Class of 2023 scholarships.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Approval, May 18 Minutes, and Consent Agenda (Items A-I)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With Vice Chair Emily Chávez absent and Jovonia Lewis participating virtually, the board approved the meeting agenda (6-0), May 18, 2023 monthly meeting minutes (6-0), and consent agenda items A through I (6-0). Alexandra Valladares noted that while consent included school nutrition contracts, broader community conversations on school nutrition remained ongoing.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public commenters included School for Creative Studies advocate Elizabeth Sims, Duke University chemistry PhD outreach co-chairs Amy Robinson and Addison Duda (offering STEM kits and school outreach, speaking at 01:15:45 due to a start-time mix-up), and School for Creative Studies educator Lavonne Barnes (speaking at 02:20:31 to oppose eliminating the school's high school grades).

agenda_items.title: Resolution Recognizing June as LGBTQ+ Pride Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members read an updated proclamation recognizing June 2023 as LGBTQ+ Pride Month, referencing the district's December 2022 LGBTQIA+ gender supports policy and criticizing over 75 anti-LGBTQ+ state bills nationwide. Alexandra Valladares moved approval and Jessica Carda-Auten seconded.

agenda_items.title: Resolution to Prioritize Public Schools in the 2023-25 Biennial State Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Umstead introduced a resolution calling on the NC General Assembly to fund teacher pay raises of at least 18% over two years, expand early childhood/NC Pre-K/Smart Start investments, and halt unlimited expansion of the Opportunity Scholarship private school voucher program (projected to cost DPS ~$6 million or 3% in state funding by 2026-27). Natalie Beyer moved approval and Alexandra Valladares seconded.

agenda_items.title: Chief of Staff: Annual Review of Purchasing and Construction Thresholds
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of Staff Tanya Giovanni and CFO Paul LeSieur presented the mandated annual review of board purchasing thresholds ($200,000 general contracts / $500,000 operations). Legal counsel and board members noted the contract spreadsheet mixed board-approved and superintendent-approved items, directing staff to return in August with a segregated, categorized report before deciding whether to lower the threshold (e.g., to $150,000).

agenda_items.title: Operation Services: Glenn Elementary School GMP Renovation and Addition Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Project Manager Kimberly Williams and Dr. LeFries presented the Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) of $57,053,519 (plus $417,541 in alternates) with Clancy & Theys and The Daniels Company (26.9% MWBE participation) for a phased 30-month occupied renovation of Glenn Elementary, noting inflation and supply-chain pressures pushed the bid above the $55 million 2022 bond estimate. Jovonia Lewis moved approval and Millicent Rogers seconded.

agenda_items.title: School Resource Officer (SRO) MOU Extension for SY 2023-24
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Administration recommended renewing the 22-SRO MOU with the Durham County Sheriff's Office unchanged for 2023-24 while awaiting the Community Safety and Wellness Task Force's October 2023 recommendations (presented by liaison Jovonia Lewis) and pursuing county funding for a Lakeview School SRO. Jovonia Lewis moved approval with the Lakeview funding follow-up and Natalie Beyer seconded; Millicent Rogers and Jessica Carda-Auten voted No over policing in schools and inability to amend the MOU mid-year.

agenda_items.title: Growing Together: Secondary Application Programs and School Boundaries
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following staff updates and public opposition from School for Creative Studies (SCS) advocate Lavonne Barnes, the board voted on the Growing Together secondary boundary and program assignment plan, which preserves SCS as a 6-8 year-round middle school while sunsetting its high school grades. Natalie Beyer moved approval and Jessica Carda-Auten seconded; Millicent Rogers and Alexandra Valladares voted No to oppose closing the district's only year-round high school.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Alexandra Valladares moved to enter closed session for the statutory purposes stated on the agenda, seconded by Jessica Carda-Auten. The board approved the motion 6-0 by roll call.

disagreements.issue: Renewal of 22-SRO Contract with Durham County Sheriff's Office for SY 2023-24
disagreements.summary: The board split 4-2 on renewing the existing School Resource Officer MOU unchanged for another school year versus withholding approval until task force reforms and stronger training/grievance accountability were added.
disagreements.side_a_position: Renew the 2023-24 SRO MOU now (and seek funding for Lakeview) while awaiting the Community Safety and Wellness Task Force's October 2023 recommendations for 2024-25.
side_a_arguments: Year-round schools open in July, requiring an active MOU so campus safety coverage does not lapse.
The Community Safety and Wellness Task Force has conducted 16 listening sessions and should finalize its recommendations before major structural changes are negotiated.
Adding an SRO at Lakeview addresses campus weapon and coverage gaps if county funding is secured.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose renewing the MOU unchanged due to concerns over policing in schools, lack of grievance/referral data, and inability to incorporate task force reforms until 2024-25.
side_b_arguments: Increased law enforcement in schools may not support the educational process, and alternative non-SRO models (such as Milwaukee) merit evaluation.
Board members had not yet received requested data on SRO grievances, discipline/law enforcement referrals, or mandatory Youth Mental Health First Aid training.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 4-2 on roll call to extend the SRO MOU for SY 2023-24 while committing to review task force recommendations once released.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 6/15/23
disagreements.issue: Growing Together Secondary Plan and Sunsetting High School Grades at School for Creative Studies
disagreements.summary: The board split 4-2 over adopting the Growing Together secondary boundary and program plan, centered on converting School for Creative Studies (SCS) from a 6-12 campus into a 6-8 year-round middle school.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt the Growing Together secondary plan converting SCS to a 6-8 year-round middle school to relieve northern/eastern growth and serve more middle schoolers.
side_a_arguments: Rapid residential growth in northern and eastern Durham requires expanding middle school year-round capacity near Holt, Eno Valley/Easley, and Oak Grove.
SCS's creative theme remains intact for grades 6-8, while the 5-year review rule allows revisiting high school options later.
disagreements.side_b_position: Reject sunsetting SCS's high school program because it serves neurodivergent and diverse learners as the district's only year-round high school.
side_b_arguments: SCS is the only year-round middle/high magnet in North Carolina and provides a small, supportive environment where struggling and neurodivergent students thrive.
Alternative land utilization or retrofitting on the Red Mill Road campus was not sufficiently explored before deciding to phase out grades 9-12.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 4-2 on roll call to adopt the Growing Together secondary plan.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 5/18/23
meetings.executive_summary: In a marathon six-and-a-half-hour meeting, the board reviewed the comprehensive Growing Together secondary assignment proposal, adopted the 2023-2028 Strategic Plan, and voted to end the district's Gaggle student surveillance contract. After hearing roughly 20 public commenters on youth safety, Title IX handling, and student privacy, the board gave detailed feedback on Growing Together—specifically asking staff to explore regionalizing the Lucas and Lakewood Montessori middle school programs ahead of a June vote. Following debate over explicitly naming Exceptional Children (EC) metrics and culturally responsive curriculum, members unanimously approved (7-0) the 2023-2028 Strategic Plan with EC inclusion edits. The board then voted 6-1 (Jovonia Lewis dissenting) to authorize terminating the Gaggle contract effective June 30, 2023—forgoing $116,371 in state grant funds over privacy, algorithmic bias, and staff workload concerns—before unanimously passing an Every Child NC resolution opposing private school vouchers (7-0) and approving the amended personnel report (6-0) after closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Celebrations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead called the meeting to order (noting Jovonia Lewis would join virtually later) and led a moment of silence. Celebrations recognized NC Science Olympiad winners, Northern High's NC Junior Chef team, Governor's School selectees, Student of the Month, Teachers of the Month (including Merrick Moore's David Brown), Lead Social Worker of the Year, and IT Director Joy Malone.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga congratulated 2023 DPS Teacher of the Year Jaira Davis and Project Search graduates, explained the district was taking extra time to finalize a fair classified salary study proposal while thanking County Manager Kimberly Sowell for recommending full funding of DPS's budget request, and announced Deputy/COO Dr. Julius Monk's upcoming departure to Guilford County.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review, April 20 Minutes, and Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With Jovonia Lewis not yet present, the board amended the agenda to add a resolution opposing private school vouchers as Item 9E (6-0), approved the April 20, 2023 monthly meeting minutes (6-0), and later approved the consent agenda unanimously (6-0 at 01:30:34).

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Roughly 20 speakers addressed the board under a two-minute limit. Students and advocates testified about delays in Title IX sexual violence investigations and weak enforcement of school-level no-contact orders, while other commenters raised concerns about student digital privacy and Gaggle monitoring.

agenda_items.title: Academic Services: Growing Together Secondary Recommendations (Information/Discussion)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Hardy, Sheena Cooper, Matthew Palmer, Dr. Julie Pack, and Director Marshall presented the secondary Growing Together proposal covering middle/high feeder alignment, Brogden DLI, Lucas Montessori, converting School for Creative Studies to 6-8, legacy/sibling/lottery rules, and bus ride-time savings. Board members questioned why Lucas and Lakewood Montessori were proposed as district-wide rather than regional lotteries, urged staff to explore regionalizing Montessori before June, and discussed DSA equity/access rules.

agenda_items.title: 2023-2028 Strategic Plan Adoption

Board members debated adding Exceptional Children (EC) students and educators to Goal 1B/3B and elevating culturally responsive curriculum in the strategy titles before voting 7-0 to adopt the plan with EC inclusion and identity-safety edits.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 5/18/23
disagreements.issue: Continuation vs. Termination of Gaggle Student Device Surveillance Contract
disagreements.summary: The board split 6-1 over terminating DPS's Gaggle monitoring contract effective June 30, 2023 and returning $116,371 in state grant funds versus keeping the software through its 2024 grant end as an added suicide-prevention layer.
disagreements.side_a_position: Terminate the Gaggle contract effective June 30, 2023 and invest effort in relationship-building, 988/tip lines, and student-centered mental health supports.
side_a_arguments: Survey and 100-day metrics did not clearly distinguish where Gaggle prevented harm versus created harm, with many PSS alerts turning out to be non-emergencies and staff spending significant after-hours time.
Gaggle raised serious student privacy concerns, chilled students from logging into school accounts on personal devices, and lacked transparent auditing for algorithmic bias.
disagreements.side_b_position: Retain Gaggle through the remainder of its grant-funded term in 2024 until an alternative safety net is established.
side_b_arguments: Gaggle provides an extra protective layer against rising youth suicidal ideation and self-harm, and 75% of surveyed contacts reported taking action on at least one safety concern they would not have otherwise known.
Returning the funds leaves a gap before additional counselors or replacement supports are in place.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 6-1 on roll call authorizing administration to terminate the Gaggle contract effective June 30, 2023.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 5/18/23
disagreements.issue: Strategic Plan Specificity on Exceptional Children (EC) Metrics and Culturally Responsive Curriculum
disagreements.summary: Board members debated how explicitly the five-year Strategic Plan goals should single out EC students, EC educators, and culturally responsive curriculum versus keeping high-level goals flexible.
disagreements.side_a_position: Add explicit EC student/educator benchmarks to Goal 1B/3A-3B and elevate 'Culturally Responsive Curriculum' as a headline strategy title.
side_a_arguments: Goal 1B explicitly broke out Black, Hispanic, and LEP students while omitting EC students, risking lower visibility and accountability for students with disabilities.
Renamings such as 'Culturally Responsive Curriculum' signal clear district values amid hostile state-level curriculum politics.
disagreements.side_b_position: Keep the high-level five-year strategic plan broad enough to remain adaptable across changing staffing shortages and avoid locking departments into narrow operational metrics.
side_b_arguments: Over-specifying single hard-to-fill roles or narrow metrics at the 30,000-foot level could lock the district in over a five-year horizon, whereas department work plans and monthly updates track disaggregated data.
Opportunity Gaps is broader than curriculum alone and already encompasses culturally responsive curriculum, teacher diversity, and discipline.
disagreements.resolution: Resolved unanimously (7-0) by adopting the plan with a directive for staff and RTI to add an appropriate EC metric in consultation with the EC department and strengthen identity-inclusion wording.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 5/4/23
meetings.executive_summary: With Chair Bettina Umstead participating virtually via Zoom, Vice Chair Emily Chávez presided over a unanimous work session focused on Durham Tech pathways, trustee appointments, and the FY 2023-24 county budget request. Durham Technical Community College President JB Buxton and Dr. Julie Pack presented plans to expand Career and College Promise dual enrollment, bond-funded allied health and life sciences facilities, and a 400-student early college model. The board unanimously reappointed Dr. Pat Ashley and appointed former DPS Chair Dr. Mike Lee to the Durham Tech Board of Trustees (7-0) while committing to develop an open application process for future appointments. Members also unanimously approved (7-0) submitting the $10.8 million FY 2023-24 local funding increase request to Durham County—centering $4.1 million for the classified salary study ($17/hour minimum) and staff raises—while directing staff to cost out $18-$20/hour county/city parity, Master's pay, EC/ESL differentials, and paid parental leave for the 2024-25 cycle.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, Amended Agenda, Minutes, and Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Emily Chávez called the work session to order with Chair Bettina Umstead joining via Zoom and led a moment of silence. The board unanimously approved (7-0) an amended agenda swapping Items 7 and 8 so the Durham Tech presentation preceded the trustee appointments, then unanimously approved the March 9 and April 6 work session minutes (7-0), heard one public commenter on youth murder cases in courtroom proceedings, and adopted the consent agenda (7-0).

agenda_items.title: Academic Services: Durham Technical Community College & DPS Career and College Promise Partnership
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham Tech President JB Buxton and Dr. Julie Pack presented expanding Career and College Promise dual enrollment, credential completion, early middle-school career planning via Zello, and expanding Middle College toward a 400-seat Early College enabled by bond-funded allied health and life sciences buildings. Board members asked about RISE placement test barriers, ESL and undocumented student access, universal pre-K early childhood pipelines, and AI/biomedical career tracks.

agenda_items.title: Board of Education: Durham Technical Community College Board of Trustees Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead nominated Dr. Pat Ashley for a new term and former DPS Chair Dr. Mike Lee to complete the late John Burness's term on the Durham Tech Board of Trustees, seconded by Natalie Beyer. Board members approved both appointments 7-0 while expressing commitment to create a transparent public application process and request regular trustee updates in the future.

agenda_items.title: Operation Services: FY 2023-24 Budget Request to Durham County ($10.8M Increase)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Paul LeSieur presented the $10.8 million local funding increase request ($9.0 million for DPS operations—anchored by $4.1 million for the classified salary study raising minimum pay to $17/hour plus 4.25% certified and 4% classified raises—and $1.8 million for charter schools) within a ~$734 million overall budget. Board members approved the $10.8 million request 7-0 without last-minute additions while requesting future costings for $18-$20/hour wage parity with the city/county, Master's pay, EC/ESL differentials, paid parental leave, and capital needs.

agenda_items.title: Operation Services: ESSER Funding Update (SY 2022-23 Q3)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Paul LeSieur reported roughly 46% of ESSER funds remained, including $300,000+ summer HVAC replacements, ~$2 million for LETRS stipends, and 119 ESSER custodial/school positions (45.5 filled at end of March). Board members pressed administration on how termed ESSER positions and programs will be assessed by October-December 2023 ahead of the September 2024 federal funding cliff.

agenda_items.title: Follow-Up Summary, Closed Session, and Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff summarized follow-up items including costing out $18-$20/hr starting pay parity, EC/ESL/Master's differentials, paid parental leave models, and analyzing ESSER-funded position outcomes. The board voted 7-0 to enter closed session and, upon returning at 03:08:02, approved the May 4, 2023 personnel report 7-0 by roll call before adjourning.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 4/20/23
meetings.executive_summary: The Board of Education navigated a five-hour-plus meeting featuring urgent public testimony on Title IX enforcement, joint action on youth gun violence, a clean annual financial audit, and major capital and strategic planning steps. During a 20-speaker public comment period, students called for faster Title IX investigations and stricter enforcement of school no-contact orders, while a DSA student cautioned against mandatory moments of silence for Day of Remembrance. The board unanimously adopted the tri-body Day of Remembrance Resolution with Durham City Council and the County Commissioners, received a clean unmodified FY 2021-22 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR) audit, and unanimously selected Monteith Construction, Balfour Beatty, and Right Build International as Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR) for the new Durham School of the Arts campus. After reviewing the draft 2023-2028 Strategic Plan with RTI and requesting quantifiable equity subgroup goals, the board entered closed session, unanimously approved the personnel report, and tabled a property acquisition item.

Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga then praised the Hillside High School job fair, noted upcoming cabinet departures (Dr. Julius Monk and Chip Sudderth), and highlighted upcoming board and cabinet LGBTQIA+ training.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Approval, March 23 Minutes, and Consent Agenda

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Approximately 20 speakers spoke under a two-minute time limit. Speakers included Dr. Wanda Boone (pledging Together for Resilient Youth partnership against youth gun violence), DSA student Kayla Scales McCoy (warning a mandatory moment of silence across schools could trigger trauma), parent Kenya Myers (seeking an independent facility for Durham School of Technology), and multiple students criticizing Title IX reporting delays and lack of enforcement of school no-contact orders.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 4/6/23
meetings.executive_summary: The board opened the evening with its FY 2023-24 budget public hearing—hearing from People's Alliance speaker Jenny Jones in support of classified raises and full EC staffing—before moving into the April 6 work session. Following unanimous approval of an amended agenda, the board reviewed the draft purpose statement and facilitator options for the LGBTQIA+ Task Force. Sharp tension surfaced during Item 7B (Day of Remembrance proposal): while Jovonia Lewis and Alexandra Valladares advocated a May 15 joint civic remembrance honoring youth lost to gun violence, Millicent Rogers and Natalie Beyer warned against 'performative' events without concrete violence-prevention policies and questioned age-appropriateness for younger grades, ending with Lewis, Rogers, and Valladares forming a committee to draft a joint resolution for April 20. disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 4/6/23
disagreements.issue: Day of Remembrance Proposal: Concrete Policy Commitments and Age-Appropriateness vs. Community Vigil
disagreements.summary: Board members clashed sharply over whether a proposed May 15 Day of Remembrance risked being 'performative' or triggering for younger students versus serving as an essential, community-requested acknowledgment of grief.
disagreements.side_a_position: Require concrete violence-prevention policies and ensure age-appropriate school implementation rather than holding a performative event or district-wide moments of silence for young children.
side_a_arguments: The board should pair any remembrance with actionable preventative measures such as SAVE clubs and public health/gun-control advocacy rather than a performative day alone.
District-wide moments of silence in elementary and middle schools may not be age-appropriate, and City Council/BOCC partners needed fuller readiness.
disagreements.side_b_position: Honor families' explicit requests for collective mourning and visibility while building joint action steps through a tri-body resolution.
side_b_arguments: Calling community-initiated mourning and vigils 'performative' dismissed real family grief and felt like a microaggression to organizers.
A joint resolution with City Council and County Commissioners can both validate community trauma and commit to concrete youth programs, summer jobs, and prevention work.
disagreements.resolution: Board formed a working committee of Jovonia Lewis, Millicent Rogers, and Alexandra Valladares to draft an action-oriented tri-body resolution with student support guidance for April 20.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 3/23/23
meetings.executive_summary: The Board of Education began the afternoon by swearing in newly appointed District 3 member Jessica Carda-Auten—marking an all-female seven-member board—before opening its monthly business meeting with condolences for Riverside and Lakeview families impacted by gun violence. Following extensive student, staff, and National Board Certified Teacher recognitions and a two-minute public comment period centered on classified staff living wages and solar energy at Northern High School, the board unanimously approved its agenda, February 23 minutes, and consent change-order report. CFO Paul LeSieur presented the Superintendent's Proposed FY 2023-24 Budget, highlighting declining enrollment projections (30,772 ADM, costing 75 state teaching positions since 2019-20), the looming September 2024 ESSER cliff, and a $10.8 million county increase request anchored by $4.1 million for the classified salary study. The board voted unanimously to approve the proposed budget for the April 6 public hearing and later approved the March 23 personnel report unanimously following closed session.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Judge Dorothy swore in newly selected District 3 board member Jessica Carda-Auten ahead of the regular session (followed by a notary swearing-in at 02:05:51), welcoming an all-female board. At 01:16:06, Chair Bettina Umstead called the monthly meeting to order and led a moment of silence for Riverside and Lakeview school communities affected by recent gun violence.

agenda_items.title: Celebrations and Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff recognized student leaders, scholarship honorees, Students of the Month, Spark Pin recipients, HR technician Sarai Jimenez, and newly certified/maintained National Board Certified Teachers and counselors. Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga then highlighted the DPS Teacher Art Gallery Showcase at the Durham Arts Council featuring 50+ works by 17 teachers and wished year-round schools a restful intercession.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Approval, February 23 Minutes, and Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved the March 23 meeting agenda (moved by Millicent Rogers, seconded by Natalie Beyer), the February 23, 2023 monthly meeting minutes (moved by Natalie Beyer, seconded by Alexandra Valladares), and later the consent agenda covering the February 2023 monthly change order report (02:54:33, moved by Natalie Beyer, seconded by Millicent Rogers).

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public speakers under a two-minute limit included an Exceptional Children instructional assistant describing classified employees working two or three jobs and struggling to afford meals, Northern High School senior Barnes advocating parking-lot solar panels at the new campus, and parents/staff urging stronger classified wage increases and addressing school lockdowns.

agenda_items.title: Operation Services: Superintendent's Proposed FY 2023-24 Budget ($10.8M Local Request)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Paul LeSieur presented the FY 2023-24 proposed budget amid declining ADM projections (30,772 vs. 32,520 in 2019-20), HB 90 K-3 class-size mandates, and ESSER's September 2024 expiration, detailing a $10.8 million county increase request ($9.0M DPS operations including $4.1M for the classified salary study plus 4.25% certified / 4% classified raises, and $1.8M charter share). Board members approved the proposed budget unanimously while requesting future analysis of salary compression, EC/ESL differential pay, paid parental leave, and mental health staffing.

meetings.title: DPS Board of Education -District 3 Candidate Selection
meetings.executive_summary: In a specially called 39-minute meeting with Alexandra Valladares joining remotely via Zoom, the six seated members of the Board of Education met to appoint a replacement for the vacant District 3 seat through June 30, 2024. After unanimously approving the agenda, board members debated the qualifications and alignment of four applicants, dividing between Kevin Primus and Jessica Carda-Auten. Valladares and Jovonia Lewis backed Primus for his data-driven focus on EC/ELL and trauma-informed metrics, extensive research network, and community coalition backing, while Natalie Beyer, Millicent Rogers, Emily Chávez, and Chair Bettina Umstead favored Carda-Auten for her public health expertise, PTA and DPS parent engagement, relationships with local officials, and collaborative approach to Growing Together. Following a coin flip to set the voting order, the board rejected Primus's nomination 2-4 and voted 4-2 to appoint Jessica Carda-Auten to the District 3 seat.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead called the special meeting to order with Alexandra Valladares participating via Zoom and led a moment of silence. On roll call, all six seated members voted unanimously (6-0) to approve the agenda.

agenda_items.title: District 3 Vacancy Deliberation and Candidate Selection
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members delivered comments weighing the four District 3 applicants before holding formal nominations determined by a coin toss (won by Kevin Primus's side to go first). On roll call votes, Alexandra Valladares's nomination of Kevin Primus failed 2-4 (Valladares and Jovonia Lewis voting Aye), and Bettina Umstead's nomination of Jessica Carda-Auten passed 4-2 (Millicent Rogers, Natalie Beyer, Emily Chávez, and Umstead voting Aye).

votes.notes: District 3 seat vacant; Alexandra Valladares participated via Zoom. Mover and seconder names not stated aloud.
votes.discussion_detail: The agenda as presented was moved and seconded, and all six seated board members voted Aye by roll call.

votes.notes: Nominations did not require a second; voting order determined by coin toss.
votes.discussion_detail: Following a coin toss setting Kevin Primus first on the ballot, Alexandra Valladares nominated Primus and voted Aye alongside Jovonia Lewis, while Millicent Rogers, Natalie Beyer, Emily Chávez, and Chair Bettina Umstead voted No, failing 2-4.

votes.item_title: Appointment of Jessica Carda-Auten to District 3 Board Seat
votes.notes: Appointed to serve the District 3 seat through June 30, 2024; nominations did not require a second.
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Bettina Umstead nominated Jessica Carda-Auten for the District 3 vacancy. On roll call, Millicent Rogers, Natalie Beyer, Emily Chávez, and Bettina Umstead voted Aye while Alexandra Valladares and Jovonia Lewis voted No, appointing Carda-Auten 4-2.

disagreements.resolution: Kevin Primus's nomination failed 2-4 and Jessica Carda-Auten's nomination passed 4-2 on roll call votes.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 3/9/23
meetings.executive_summary: At its March 9, 2023 work session, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education unanimously adopted a resolution opposing North Carolina House Bill 187 (Equality in Education), approved a negotiated contract for a new financial and human resources ERP system, and proclaimed March 2023 as Arts in Our Schools Month. The board received an update on upcoming two-part LGBTQIA+ governance trainings scheduled for April 21 and May 19, 2023, along with Strategic Plan Priority 4 (family and community engagement) and Priority 5 (fiscal and operational responsibility, including transportation and disparity study needs) updates. The board also unanimously approved a $1,500 ESSER-funded retention bonus (about $7.5 million total) to be paid in September 2023 to returning employees, and approved the March 9, 2023 personnel report following closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, Agenda Approval, and Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead called the work session to order, recognized the Spanish interpreters, and led a moment of silence. The board approved the evening's agenda and the February 9, 2023 work session minutes, with one board member (Jovonia Lewis) noted as arriving later due to a prior commitment.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment and Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Two speakers addressed the board during public comment: Minister Paul Scott urged the board to adopt the resolution opposing House Bill 187 ahead of its legislative committee hearing, and Kevin Primus expressed support for the Arts in Our Schools Month proclamation and urged integration of arts across core subjects while commenting on a recent community incident. Following public comment, the board approved the consent agenda without discussion.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Opposing North Carolina House Bill 187
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members read aloud in full a resolution opposing House Bill 187 ('Equality in Education'), arguing the bill would restrict educators from teaching accurate U.S. and North Carolina history regarding slavery, Jim Crow, women's suffrage, and systemic racism, and reaffirming DPS's equity commitments and legislative priorities. Board members noted minor grammatical edits to be cleaned up with the board clerk without altering content.

agenda_items.title: Contract for New Financial and Human Resources (ERP) System
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of Staff Tanya Giovanni presented the finalized legal terms of the contract for DPS's new financial and human resources ERP system following negotiations with board attorneys and staff. She noted that no substantive or financial terms had changed since CFO Paul LeSieur's February 9 presentation and requested formal board approval of the finalized contract.

agenda_items.title: Update on LGBTQIA+ Board and Cabinet Training
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of Staff Tanya Giovanni and Vice Chair Emily Chávez presented logistical plans for two governance trainings (101 on April 21, 2023 and 201 on May 19, 2023) at the Minnie Forte-Brown Staff Development Center, costing roughly $5,600 for speakers including NSBA legal counsel and Gender Spectrum. Board members discussed whether to invite the LGBTQIA+ task force once finalized and agreed to livestream the educational lecture portions with Spanish interpretation while keeping interactive board/cabinet workshop segments unstreamed.

agenda_items.title: Arts in Our Schools Month Proclamation

agenda_items.title: Strategic Plan Priority 4 Update: School, Family, and Community Engagement

Board members—including Jovonia Lewis, who arrived during the discussion—pressed for a partnership evaluation rubric, expanded Multilingual Resource Center (MRC) capacity, college access partnerships, and school-level communications toolkits for Growing Together.

agenda_items.title: ESSER-Funded $1,500 Employee Retention Bonus for September 2023

meetings.title: DPS Board of Education -District 3 Candidate Interviews
meetings.executive_summary: On March 8, 2023, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education held public candidate interviews to fill the vacant District 3 seat created by former Vice Chair Matt Sears's resignation. Four eligible District 3 applicants—Jessica Carter-Oton, April Lawson Day, Kevin Primus, and Jessica Freelander—delivered timed 10-minute presentations addressing four standard board prompts on superintendent evaluation metrics, equity, engaging marginalized communities, and school safety, followed by two-minute responses on one self-selected and one randomly drawn policy topic. Vice Chair Emily Chávez participated virtually while the remaining five board members attended in person; no board deliberations or votes occurred, with the appointment vote scheduled for a special called meeting on March 16, 2023.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Interview Format Overview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead opened the meeting, recognized Vice Chair Emily Chávez attending virtually, and read aloud the four standardized interview prompts and the list of policy topics for the two-minute impromptu segments. She noted that board members would listen without asking live follow-up questions during the presentations.

agenda_items.title: District 3 Candidate Interview: Jessica Carter-Oton
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jessica Carter-Oton, a UNC qualitative public health researcher and Lakewood Elementary parent, emphasized closing the opportunity gap with disaggregated data, recruiting Black and Latinx educators, expanding enrollment, and addressing magnet-versus-base resource inequities through Growing Together. She advocated data-driven, non-fear-based school safety measures, restorative justice fidelity, and full implementation of the classified staff salary study.

agenda_items.title: District 3 Candidate Interview: April Lawson Day
agenda_items.discussion_summary: April Lawson Day, a DPS parent with legal and government experience, highlighted disproportionate discipline for students of color and students with disabilities, advocated proactive mental health screenings, and proposed evaluating the superintendent on strategic, cultural, and managerial leadership. In her two-minute topics, she called for competitive compensation including for substitutes and part-time staff and balanced budgets across secondary Growing Together boundary planning.

agenda_items.title: District 3 Candidate Interview: Kevin Primus
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Kevin Primus, a father of five DPS students, former Wake County teacher, and Riverside High School Improvement Team member, proposed evaluating the superintendent on Growing Together community engagement, educator recruitment, and trauma-informed training to close the 'engagement gap.' He stressed stronger feeder-school academic alignment between middle and high schools and expanding pipelines with Durham Tech and NCCU for bilingual, EC, and educators of color.

agenda_items.title: District 3 Candidate Interview: Jessica Freelander
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a brief recess, Jessica Freelander, a nine-year former teacher and advanced academic coordinator at Riverside High School, focused on disproportionate suspension rates, charter school impacts, dual-identified EC/ESL service gaps, and expanding honors/advanced course access for historically marginalized students. She emphasized mental health and social-emotional safety as well as job satisfaction and financial support for educator recruitment and retention.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 2/9/23
meetings.executive_summary: At a nearly seven-hour work session on February 9, 2023—opened with board tributes and a moment of silence after another student death from gun violence impacting Hillside High School—the Durham Public Schools Board of Education accepted Vice Chair Matt Sears's January 31 resignation and experienced a sharp three-round deadlock before electing Emily Chávez as Vice Chair on a 4-2 vote over Jovonia Lewis. The board unanimously approved the District 3 vacancy appointment timeline, a CROWN Act Week resolution, a Leandro funding letter to Governor Roy Cooper, and a CTE Month proclamation, and heard presentations on Equity & Professional Learning and Safety & Security, including the district-wide launch of Gaggle student device monitoring. Later in the evening, the board unanimously approved Superintendent Pascal Mubenga's spending plan for the $18 million MacKenzie Scott donation ($14.5 million net of $3.5 million legally owed to charter schools) after amending it to separate out the $1 million teacher-housing reserve pending an MOU, and also approved the ERP financial/HR system contract subject to board attorney sign-off.

agenda_items.title: Opening Remarks on Hillside High School Tragedy, Agenda Approval, and Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members offered emotional tributes and called for community-wide action on gun violence, mental health counselors, and gun-storage safety following another student death impacting Hillside High School, followed by a moment of silence. The board amended the agenda to add the CROWN Act Week resolution and an Every Child NC Leandro letter, and unanimously approved the January 12, 2023 work session minutes.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public commenters raised concerns over Senate Bill 49 (Parents' Bill of Rights) and student privacy, grieved the Hillside student shooting while urging action on youth safety, and sharply criticized Matt Sears's mid-term resignation to join the DPS Foundation—calling for transparency around board members leaving office for a partner organization receiving district funds.

agenda_items.title: Acceptance of Matt Sears's Resignation and Election of Vice Chair
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously accepted Matt Sears's resignation effective January 31, 2023. Following a coin toss to set voting order after simultaneous nominations of Emily Chávez (by Natalie Beyer) and Jovonia Lewis (by Alexandra Valladares), the board deadlocked 3-3 on Chávez in Round 1 and 3-3 on Lewis in Round 2 amid candid debate over board exclusion, rotational leadership, and experience, before electing Emily Chávez Vice Chair 4-2 on Round 3 when Chair Bettina Umstead switched her vote to break the tie.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Resignation Passed 6-0; Vice Chair: Chávez 3-3, Lewis 3-3, Chávez Elected 4-2

agenda_items.title: District 3 Board Vacancy Appointment Process and Conflict-of-Interest Policy Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members reviewed and approved the application statement of interest and 60-day appointment schedule (due Feb. 27, interviews March 7-8), adding an equity question and preferred pronouns field. Jovonia Lewis asked board counsel whether an MOU or waiting period should govern board members departing for the DPS Foundation to avoid the appearance of conflict of interest, prompting Natalie Beyer to defend Matt Sears's and former member Mike Lee/Casein's ethics while supporting clarity.

agenda_items.title: CROWN Act Week Resolution, Every Child NC Leandro Letter, and CTE Month Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board read and unanimously adopted the CROWN Act Week resolution affirming natural hair and prohibiting race-based hair discrimination, approved sending Every Child NC's Leandro funding letter urging Governor Roy Cooper to protect recurring years 2 and 3 Leandro investments from budget cuts, and adopted Dr. Julie Pack's proclamation declaring February 2023 Career and Technical Education (CTE) Month.

agenda_items.title: Academic Services Updates: Equity & Professional Learning and Safety, Security & Gaggle
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Kelvin Bullock presented updates on the consolidated Office of Equity and Professional Learning, including LETRS literacy training, 12 beginning-teacher mentors, and Policy 1735/1900 training. Safety Director Eva Howard, IT Director Joy Malone, and Dr. Laverne Maddox-Perry then detailed campus security cameras, Zscaler web filtering, 17 Sheriff's Office SROs, and the January 23, 2023 district-wide launch of Gaggle 24/7 monitoring (which reviewed 6,578 items in its first seven days and includes 911 wellness-check protocols when families cannot be reached).

agenda_items.title: MacKenzie Scott $18 Million Donation Spending Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Pascal Mubenga and cabinet leaders presented the $18 million MacKenzie Scott donation allocation—subtracting $3.5 million legally owed to charter schools and dedicating $8.22 million to academics (summer institute PD, Growing Together elementary arts/STEM/world languages, CTE buses/fire truck/ambulance/food truck, $500,000 Family Engagement Center, $280,000 DPS Foundation Whole School Initiative, and $1 million teacher housing reserve), $2.5 million to HR pipelines, $1.5 million to transportation/white fleet EVs, $1.28 million to school support, and $1 million to emergency radios. After Jovonia Lewis objected to placing the $1 million teacher housing reserve with the DPS Foundation without an RFP, the board amended the motion to separate the $1 million housing item pending a future MOU/partner decision.

agenda_items.title: FY 2023-24 Operations Budget Preview and Financial/HR ERP System Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Although board members moved to defer detailed budget discussion due to the late hour, CFO Paul LeSieur briefly reviewed deferred budget items, projected state salary/retirement increases, enrollment loss impacts (24 lost state teaching positions), and board questions on funding the classified salary study versus a potential local parental-leave working group. The board then unanimously approved the new financial and human resources (ERP) system contract subject to board attorney approval.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board entered closed session at 06:14:47 and returned at 06:48:56, unanimously approving the February 9, 2023 personnel report before adjourning.

votes.discussion_detail: Added CROWN Act Week resolution (6C) and Every Child NC Leandro letter to Governor Cooper (6D); seconded simultaneously by Millicent Rogers and Jovonia Lewis.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved January 12, 2023 work session minutes as presented.

votes.discussion_detail: Accepted Matt Sears's resignation from the District 3 seat effective January 31, 2023 to join the DPS Foundation.

votes.notes: Nominations do not require a second under board policy.

votes.notes: Chair Bettina Umstead announced the 3-3 tie and proceeded to Round 3.
votes.discussion_detail: Second voice roll call on Jovonia Lewis following speeches by both candidates and Alexandra Valladares; also resulted in a 3-3 tie.

votes.discussion_detail: Bettina Umstead shifted her vote to Aye in the third round to break the 3-3 deadlock and elect Emily Chávez as Vice Chair, noting both nominees were qualified and the board needed to move forward with its agenda.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved posting the District 3 statement of interest (with added equity question and pronoun field) due February 27, with interviews on March 7-8, 2023.

votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the CROWN Act Week resolution affirming natural hair and prohibiting race-based hair discrimination in DPS schools.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved sending the Every Child NC letter urging Governor Roy Cooper to protect recurring years 2 and 3 Leandro investments in the state base budget.

votes.discussion_detail: Proclaimed February 1-28, 2023 as Career and Technical Education Month.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved acceptance and allocation of the $18 million MacKenzie Scott donation ($14.5M after $3.5M charter share), amended to separate out the $1 million teacher-housing reserve from the DPS Foundation pending a board-approved MOU and partner review.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved the contract for the new financial and human resource system subject to final contract language review by the board attorney.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 2/9/23
disagreements.issue: Election of Board Vice Chair and Board Communication/Leadership Process
disagreements.summary: Following Matt Sears's resignation, the board split 3-3 across two rounds between nominees Emily Chávez and Jovonia Lewis amid pointed debate over rotational leadership, prior experience, and alleged cliques/exclusionary communication before Chair Bettina Umstead broke the tie for Chávez on the third ballot.
disagreements.side_a_position: Elect Emily Chávez as Vice Chair to bring new energy, rotational leadership, and collaborative focus
side_a_arguments: Chávez brought budget advisory co-chair experience, an intersectional equity lens, and strong relationships with commissioners and colleagues.
Supporting Chávez aligned with rotational leadership and moving the board's agenda forward after two deadlocked ballots.
disagreements.side_b_position: Elect Jovonia Lewis based on three years of board experience and push back against perceived pre-arranged cliques and exclusionary communication
side_b_arguments: Lewis argued that after three years on the board—including pandemic leadership and prior service—experience and transparency should outweigh experimentation, noting Beyer had previously said she lacked experience in her first year.
Valladares criticized perceived pre-arranged whip counts, side meetings with partners like the DPS Foundation and Self-Help, and inequitable communication excluding certain board members.
disagreements.resolution: After Round 1 (Chávez) and Round 2 (Lewis) both tied 3-3, Bettina Umstead switched from voting against both nominees to voting Aye for Emily Chávez in Round 3, electing Chávez 4-2; Valladares requested Policy Committee review of Policy 220 officer terms.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 2/9/23
disagreements.issue: Board Member Resignations for DPS Foundation Roles and Conflict-of-Interest Guidelines
disagreements.summary: Following public criticism of Matt Sears resigning to join the DPS Foundation shortly after another former member did the same, board members differed on whether to pursue MOU/policy guardrails on board-to-foundation transitions versus defending former members' ethics.
disagreements.side_a_position: Explore MOU or board policy guidelines (such as recusal during interviews or a cooling-off period) to prevent the appearance of conflicts of interest
side_a_arguments: The public raised concerns about two board members stepping down to work at the DPS Foundation while participating in budget and housing discussions involving the foundation.
Clearer notice or cooling-off rules in an MOU could protect public trust without implying wrongdoing.
disagreements.side_b_position: Defend the ethical record of former members and avoid implying misconduct or adopting overly broad restrictions
side_b_arguments: Board counsel (Tharrington Smith) confirmed no legal conflict existed and both former members stepped down voluntarily to avoid even the appearance of conflict.
Legal counsel cautioned against foundation-specific rules that could hinder employment or complicate partnerships with aligned nonprofits.
disagreements.resolution: No formal motion was taken on an MOU change; later in the meeting, Lewis's request to separate the $1 million teacher-housing reserve from the DPS Foundation in the MacKenzie Scott grant motion was adopted unanimously.
